### F01 — CRITICAL — Project status

- **Original claim:** The architecture is complete / validated / Q1-ready.
- **Evidence:** MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md:230-239; 27-file inventory: no .py engine, training outputs, tests or own backtest results
- **Assessment:** Planning artifacts and a Pine indicator exist; completion checkmarks do not establish execution or empirical validity.
- **Correction:** Treat all pillars as proposed until their acceptance tests pass.

### F02 — CRITICAL — Publication

- **Original claim:** This will be a Q1 paper if framed as an Oxford extension.
- **Evidence:** Q1_PEER_REVIEW_REJECTION_AUDIT.md; RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md:1858-1894
- **Assessment:** Venue quartiles, novelty and acceptance are not established by phrasing, a positive Sharpe increment or combining familiar components. ICAIF is a conference, not a Q1-ranked journal.
- **Correction:** Define a falsifiable contribution and compare closest work; verify any journal quartile by year/category/source separately.

### F03 — CRITICAL — Prior work

- **Original claim:** Wood et al. explicitly documented intraday liquidity-absorption failure / adaptation in fewer than five bars.
- **Evidence:** Wood PDF v2 physical pp. 2, 15; full text searched
- **Assessment:** The paper describes cross-attentive regime contexts and suggests cryptocurrencies/context construction as future directions. It does not establish the claimed 15m absorption failure or guarantee sub-five-bar adaptation.
- **Correction:** Replace the alleged documented limitation with a hypothesis and test it.

### F04 — HIGH — Prior work

- **Original claim:** Order flow + news + few-shot prediction is a new capability by itself.
- **Evidence:** CAMEF arXiv:2502.04592v3 and DOI 10.1145/3711896.3736872; Deng et al. arXiv:2407.09003v1; SSRN 10.2139/ssrn.7356724 abstract
- **Assessment:** Macroeconomic multimodal forecasting, news-based few-shot prediction, and 15m meta-labeling with OI have related prior work. They are not identical to the proposed BTC task, but defeat a broad first-ever claim.
- **Correction:** Distinguish temporal decision availability, adaptation mechanism, target and evaluation rather than the ingredient list.

### F05 — HIGH — 1

- **Original claim:** All prices are I(1), hence ERM fails and few-shot learning is necessary.
- **Evidence:** MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md:44-49; local Brooks KB unit-root passages
- **Assessment:** A unit root in price levels is not identical to drift of the predictive conditional distribution. The premise does not prove every static model fails or that few-shot adaptation is uniquely necessary.
- **Correction:** Use empirical drift/structural-break diagnostics and compare retrained, rolling and static baselines.

### F06 — HIGH — 1

- **Original claim:** H0 contains p >= .05, while H1 contains p < .01 and a guaranteed drawdown reduction.
- **Evidence:** MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md:39-42
- **Assessment:** p-values are test outcomes, not population hypotheses. Several metric/threshold conditions invite post-hoc success selection.
- **Correction:** Preregister one primary estimand and material improvement threshold; report other metrics as secondary.

### F07 — CRITICAL — 2

- **Original claim:** The written CE formula matches the supplied Pine script.
- **Evidence:** chandelier_exit.pine:7-9,20-31; MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md:55-63; TradingView ATR documentation
- **Assessment:** Pine uses ta.atr(length) with length=22 and recursive ratcheted stops. The dossier uses a 14-period simple average and omits the stop ratcheting recurrences.
- **Correction:** Use Wilder/RMA ATR(22), identical extrema, nz/initialization and recursive stop logic; compare against a real exported TradingView fixture before claiming parity.

### F08 — HIGH — 2

- **Original claim:** awaitBarConfirmation makes every plotted state and label confirmed-only.
- **Evidence:** chandelier_exit.pine:39-56
- **Assessment:** The confirmation flag gates alert conditions; it is not applied to every calculation or plotted label.
- **Correction:** Evaluate Python candidates only on completed bars and validate confirmed alerts rather than intrabar plot changes.

### F09 — HIGH — 2

- **Original claim:** Session VWAP z-score is essential, bounded to [-3,3], and prevents top-buying.
- **Evidence:** RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md:1775-1779,1833-1850; MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md:66-70
- **Assessment:** A z-score is not naturally bounded and does not prove reversal/overvaluation. ATR-normalized distance and VWAP-standard-deviation distance are different features. Claimed latency/edge is unmeasured.
- **Correction:** Treat VWAP as an optional ablation; specify denominator, UTC anchor, zero-variance handling and any deliberate clipping.

### F10 — HIGH — 2

- **Original claim:** Guéant-Royer and Petukhina validate the stated 2-sigma and weekly-VWAP trading rules.
- **Evidence:** Guéant-Royer full text, DOI 10.1137/130924676; Petukhina DOI 10.1080/1351847x.2020.1789684 metadata
- **Assessment:** Guéant-Royer studies optimal VWAP execution and guaranteed VWAP contracts, not the asserted CE reversal threshold. Petukhina metadata identifies intraday crypto trading patterns; the weekly Monday-anchor rule is not substantiated by retrieved evidence.
- **Correction:** Cite only supported claims; mark threshold/weekly-anchor benefits as hypotheses or remove them.

### F11 — MEDIUM — 2 / Data

- **Original claim:** OHLCV gives exact session trade-price VWAP variance.
- **Evidence:** Binance public-data README kline schema; DATASET_COLLECTION_SPECIFICATION.md
- **Assessment:** Session sum(quote_volume)/sum(volume) can provide the trade-volume-weighted mean, subject to source rounding. A full trade-price second moment is not in klines, so a bar-price weighted standard deviation is an approximation.
- **Correction:** Name and document the bar-price variance approximation; guard zero volume/variance.

### F12 — HIGH — 3

- **Original claim:** Kline delta proves whale/institutional absorption.
- **Evidence:** DATASET_COLLECTION_SPECIFICATION.md:62-79; MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md:83-99; Binance public-data README
- **Assessment:** 2*taker_buy_volume-volume is valid executed aggressor-volume delta, not trader identity or intent. Price/delta divergence is a descriptive feature, not proof of absorption by institutions.
- **Correction:** Use neutral names and test predictive contribution; avoid smart-money labels.

### F13 — HIGH — 3

- **Original claim:** volume/count identifies whale blocks and per-trade whale delta.
- **Evidence:** DATASET_COLLECTION_SPECIFICATION.md:77-79; MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md:161-169
- **Assessment:** An average executed-trade size cannot recover the trade-size distribution, original parent order, cancellations or participant identity. A >1 BTC whale fraction cannot be reconstructed from aggregate klines.
- **Correction:** Drop the whale feature from the kline-only contract; acquire a scoped trade tape only if that separate hypothesis is justified.

### F14 — HIGH — 3

- **Original claim:** Executed taker flow makes the strategy immune to spoofing; 1-Trades/Quotes detects cancellations.
- **Evidence:** MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md:94-99; RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md:1235,1272-1305
- **Assessment:** Executed-volume data does not contain order-level cancellations, and quote updates are not equivalent to canceled orders. Market impact of manipulation is not eliminated by using a trade tape.
- **Correction:** Remove immunity/detection guarantees; treat validated cancellation detection as a distinct project requiring appropriate event-level data and labels.

### F15 — MEDIUM — 3

- **Original claim:** Top accounts vs global accounts identifies institutions vs retail; price+OI proves accumulation.
- **Evidence:** DATASET_COLLECTION_SPECIFICATION.md:89-101; official Binance connector source
- **Assessment:** Account ratios are venue-defined cohorts, not verified identities. OI is not net directional buying; interpreting a joint price/OI movement is a hypothesis.

- **Original claim:** A spike in event-window variance proves causality.
- **Evidence:** MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md:123-125
- **Assessment:** Variance association around an event does not establish a causal effect or eliminate simultaneous-event confounding and endogenous order flow.
- **Correction:** Use predictive language unless an explicit identification design and assumptions are justified.

### F22 — CRITICAL — 5

- **Evidence:** DATASET_COLLECTION_SPECIFICATION.md:129-139; MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md:134-155
- **Assessment:** A path through -1.1 ATR then +2 ATR qualifies for a sweep but also breaches the collapse/market stop. A +2 ATR winner with 0.6 ATR retracement falls between clean and sweep definitions. Shorts and precedence need explicit treatment.
- **Correction:** Define exclusive first-hit outcomes first; keep path descriptors separate from each execution policy’s actual P&L.

### F23 — CRITICAL — 5 / Execution

- **Original claim:** 15m OHLC proves TP-before-SL and limit-fill ordering.
- **Evidence:** DATASET_COLLECTION_SPECIFICATION.md:127-139; proposed hybrid execution policy
- **Assessment:** Both barriers can be touched within one candle without known event order. Neither a touch nor one-tick penetration is a queue-fill guarantee.
- **Correction:** Use finer-resolution data, retain an ambiguity flag and predefine conservative resolution; later compare limit fills to real executions.

### F24 — CRITICAL — 6

- **Original claim:** The proposed prototypical MLP is simply the implemented X-Trend extension.
- **Evidence:** MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md:171-183; Wood v2 physical p.2; Snell arXiv:1703.05175v2 abstract
- **Assessment:** The proposal is a three-linear-layer prototype classifier, whereas X-Trend uses cross-attention over regime sequences. They are distinct model families.
- **Correction:** Choose one main model explicitly; treat X-Trend and prototypical networks as separate baselines/candidates.

### F25 — CRITICAL — 6

- **Original claim:** Any recent examples can populate the support set immediately.
- **Evidence:** proposed H=8 labels and class support centroids; MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md:178-183
- **Assessment:** A support example’s future-dependent label must have finished before the query decision. Support selection, clustering/change-point detection and scaling can leak future information.
- **Correction:** Enforce support.label_end < query.decision_at and fit all selection/normalization on past data only.

### F26 — HIGH — 6

- **Original claim:** A fixed three-class embedding automatically establishes a few-shot adaptation contribution.
- **Evidence:** MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md:159-186
- **Assessment:** Episodes, task/regime identity, held-out regimes, number of shots and support update budget are unspecified. It may reduce to supervised metric learning plus nearest prototypes.
- **Correction:** Define the adaptation task and compare equal-information rolling, retrieval and supervised baselines.

### F27 — HIGH — 6

- **Original claim:** Distance thresholding is a conformal gate with guaranteed abstention reliability.
- **Evidence:** MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md:185-186
- **Assessment:** No nonconformity score, calibration split, alpha or applicable coverage assumptions are specified. The threshold rule is a heuristic rejection gate.
- **Correction:** Rename it or supply a separately justified, time-aware conformal calibration protocol.

### F28 — HIGH — 7

- **Original claim:** A class-weighted cross-entropy plus unspecified drawdown penalty enforces prop-firm safety.
- **Evidence:** MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md:196-200
- **Assessment:** A sequential equity/position process and differentiable objective are not defined. Mini-batch classification cannot alone guarantee drawdown, daily loss or broker compliance.
- **Correction:** Start with a simple prediction loss and a deterministic risk-control layer; verify actual firm rules separately.

### F29 — CRITICAL — 8

- **Original claim:** N=6,k=2 CPCV gives 15 full backtest paths and guarantees live no-lookahead.
- **Evidence:** MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md:206-210; tool calculation: 15 splits, 5 recombined paths
- **Assessment:** 15 is the split count, not the number of full recombined paths. Retrospective CPCV can train on dates later than a test block; it is not a substitute for deployment-faithful forward testing.
- **Correction:** Use nested chronological walk-forward as primary, exact label-interval purging, and CPCV only as a clearly labeled supplementary retrospective analysis.

### F30 — CRITICAL — 8 / Execution

- **Original claim:** 4bps taker/2bps maker and one fixed tick adequately model all costs and split-order fills.
- **Evidence:** MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md:212-216; hybrid policy in project notes
- **Assessment:** Fees are charged on applicable entries and exits; spreads, funding, latency, gaps, queue risk and partial/unfilled orders also matter. Fixed USD0.50 tick and universal fee-tier claims are not verified.
- **Correction:** Use actual contract/fee schedules or labeled conservative scenarios; model both legs and stress costs. Keep market-only execution for the initial baseline.

### F31 — HIGH — 8

- **Original claim:** A positive shuffled-label Sharpe proves leakage, and a DSR p<.01 gate by itself validates the edge.
- **Evidence:** MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md:218-226; DSR DOI metadata 10.3905/jpm.2014.40.5.094
- **Assessment:** Positive performance can arise from drift/chance under a null. Naive permutations destroy temporal dependence. DSR needs correct multiple-trial, dependence, moment and sample treatment, not just a named threshold.
- **Correction:** Use a valid dependence-preserving null distribution plus direct timing/causality unit tests; document every selection trial and confidence interval.

### F32 — CRITICAL — Citation integrity

- **Original claim:** SSRN 7356724 is peer-reviewed evidence of >40% Sharpe improvement from OI meta-labeling.
- **Evidence:** BINANCE_DATA_AND_BASE_PAPER.md:60-63; Crossref posted-content record and JATS abstract
- **Assessment:** The retrieved abstract reports weak discrimination, contract-dependent signs, and no paired 95% interval excluding zero under either seed. It is a working-paper record, not established peer-reviewed proof of universal improvement.
- **Correction:** Correct the quoted finding, type and uncertainty; preserve the negative evidence.

### F33 — HIGH — Citation integrity

- **Evidence:** 86 unique local DOI tokens inventoried; bounded 50-record lookup; SSRN 10.2139/ssrn.3607074 unresolved in this pass
- **Assessment:** Metadata resolution is separate from identity matching, publication status and claim support. Residual citations and claimed metrics need source-level verification.
- **Correction:** Use the saved ledger; retain unresolved metadata as [CITATION NEEDED] and never promote discovery manifests to evidence automatically.

- **Original claim:** ETH/SOL transfer is mandatory and already collected / exactly matches the Oxford protocol.
- **Evidence:** DATASET_COLLECTION_SPECIFICATION.md:143-150; 27-file inventory; no ETH/SOL market-data artifacts
- **Assessment:** Cross-asset transfer can improve external validity, but is optional and uncollected. Overlapping BTC training dates with test-asset dates are not automatically temporal OOS.
- **Correction:** Respect the BTC-first scope; add cross-asset tests only after approval, with frozen dates and adaptation budgets.

### F35 — HIGH — Metrics

- **Original claim:** PF>=1.6, win rate>=45%, MDD<=4%, abstention>=50% demonstrate a Q1/institutional edge.
- **Evidence:** PROJECT_GOAL.md; RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md; computed gross 45%-at-2R expectancy=0.35R before costs
- **Assessment:** These are proposed engineering targets, not observed results or publication criteria. Aggregate MDD differs from daily loss, and abstention over all signals differs from filtering false signals.
- **Correction:** Report traded sample sizes, coverage, uncertainty, risk/exposure matched baselines and net returns; keep research conclusions independent of profit targets.

      "short-container-title": [],
      "abstract": "<jats:p>This study evaluates an interpretable meta-labeling framework for intraday futures trend following, in which a deterministic moving-average rule generates candidate crossover events and an XGBoost secondary classifier filters them. The evaluation uses 15-minute data from five Chinese futures contracts spanning commodity and equity-index markets. Six z-scored predictors describe the local state; one predictor is the bar-level percentage change in open interest. Triple-barrier labels (TP=1.0%, SL=0.6%, H=60) drive a five-fold purged walk-forward out-of-sample evaluation with primary seed-42 and a pre-specified robustness seed-2024, under a pre-specified aggregate 4-bps round-trip cost assumption. Shared-target ROC-AUC values cluster near 0.5 across contracts and classifiers, indicating weak rank-order discrimination between TP-labeled and non-TP-labeled candidate events. Under the primary seed, the Meta-XGB event-level Ret/MDD difference versus Raw-MA is positive for C and IC and negative for RB, AU and TA. None of the five paired stationary-bootstrap 95% confidence intervals at expected block length ℓ = 20 excludes zero. Under the pre-specified robustness seed, RB and TA retain negative point-estimate signs and C retains a positive sign, while AU and IC change sign; no paired 95% interval excludes zero under either seed. At τ = 0.50, Meta-XGB accepts only 1.44%-6.76% of candidate events. SHAP attribution identifies which predictors the fitted model uses, and ablation tests incremental economic contribution. Open-interest changes are influential model inputs in several contracts, but their incremental economic contribution is contract-dependent and not uniformly positive. The evidence supports meta-labeling as an interpretable contract-dependent decision-support layer rather than as a universally performance-improving filter.</jats:p>",

        ]
      },
      "abstract": "<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>\n                  <jats:p>Fractional trading has emerged as an opportunity for investors to invest in fractions of shares, enabling access to high-priced stocks even with small budgets, and thus reaching a bigger investment community. Aside from the inventory risk faced by all market makers, providers of fractional trading are unable to perfectly hedge their positions and therefore need to forecast retail investors’ order flow over short time horizons to manage their market risk. We develop machine learning models to predict trading activity in fractional trading using time series data on investor holdings of a large set of securities across different sectors combined with daily news sentiment indicators. Our approach proceeds in two stages. First, securities are grouped into clusters with similar trading patterns, and representative firms are selected from each cluster. Second, trading activity is modeled using long short-term memory (LSTM) neural networks augmented with sentiment features. The results show that fractional trading activity can be modeled with meaningful predictive accuracy and that incorporating news sentiment improves LSTM performance in most cases. In two stylised examples, we demonstrate approaches to hedging and market risk management using the LSTM predictions. Feature importance analysis using methods from explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) identifies the primary drivers of trading activity.</jats:p>",

      "abstract": "<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>\n                  <jats:p>\n                    Spot Ether exchange-traded funds (ETFs) gave regulated investors direct access to the second-largest cryptocurrency in July 2024. We ask whether this form of institutionalization changed the speed and state dependence of Ethereum's response to scheduled macroeconomic news. We align 84 U.S. CPI releases from 2019 to March 2026 with hourly prices, lagged on-chain network activity, and daily spot-ETF flows, and estimate intraday event-study regressions in which the inflation-surprise response is conditioned on the network state. The primary outcome is Ethereum's four-hour return relative to Bitcoin, which differences out the dominant common cryptocurrency component; a rolling market-model abnormal return provides an alternative benchmark. Before the launch, network activity does not materially condition relative inflation pricing. In the ETF era the interaction turns negative, with a pooled change of − 1.13 percentage points (HC3\n                    <jats:italic>p</jats:italic>\n                    = 0.026) that survives wild-bootstrap inference, a max-T adjustment across five horizons, leave-one-announcement diagnostics, and a placebo on pre-announcement returns. The same pattern appears in market-model abnormal returns. The change is concentrated in the four-hour window: it is absent in the release hour and dissipates by 24 hours. Within the ETF era, higher lagged ETF-flow intensity further strengthens the negative response to inflation surprises, although this mechanism test rests on only 18 post-launch announcements. Institutionalization therefore appears to reorganize short-horizon price discovery in digital assets rather than to raise unconditional macro sensitivity, a distinction that daily-frequency designs cannot detect.\n                  </jats:p>",

      "abstract": "<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>In textbook models of exchange rate determination, the news contained in public information announcements is directly impounded into prices with there being no role for trading in this process of information assimilation. This paper directly tests this theoretical result using transaction level exchange rate return and trading data and a sample of scheduled macroeconomic announcements. The main result of the paper is that even information that is publicly and simultaneously released to all market participants is partially impounded into prices via the key micro level price determinant—order flow. We quantify the role that order flow plays and find that approximately one third of price-relevant information is incorporated via the trading process.</jats:p>",
      "DOI": "10.1017/s0022109000003598",

      "abstract": "<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>\n                  <jats:p>The objective of this paper is to provide a deeper insight into the links between financial markets and the real economy. To that end, we study the short-term anticipation and response of U.S. stock, Treasury, and corporate bond markets to the first release of surprise U.S. macroeconomic information. Specifically, we focus on the impact of these announcements not only on the level, but also on the volatility and comovement of those assets’ returns. We do so by estimating several extensions of the parsimonious multivariate GARCH-DCC model of Engle (2002) for the excess holding-period returns on seven portfolios of these asset classes. We find that both the process of price formation in each of those financial markets and their interaction appear to be driven by fundamentals. Yet our analysis reveals a statistically and economically significant dichotomy between the reaction of the stock and bond markets to the arrival of unexpected fundamental information. We also show that the conditional mean, volatility, and comovement among stock, Treasury, and corporate bond returns react asymmetrically to the information content of these surprise announcements. Overall, the above results shed new light on the mechanisms by which new information is incorporated into prices within and across U.S. financial markets.</jats:p>",

      "abstract": "<jats:p>We examine stock index futures and Treasury futures around the release time of 30 U.S. macroeconomic announcements. Nine of the 20 announcements that move markets show evidence of substantial informed trading before the official release time. Prices begin to move in the “correct” direction approximately 30 minutes before the release time. The preannouncement price drift accounts on average for approximately 40% of the total price adjustment. This implies that some traders have private information about macroeconomic fundamentals. Preannouncement drift might originate from a combination of information leakage and superior forecasting that incorporates proprietary data.</jats:p>",

      "abstract": "<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>We propose a method of incorporating macroeconomic news into a predictive model for forecasting prices of crude oil futures contracts. Since these futures contracts are more liquid than the underlying commodity itself, accurate forecasting of their prices is of great value to multiple categories of market participants. We utilize the Kalman filtering framework for forecasting arbitrage-free (futures) prices and assume that the volatility of oil (futures) price is influenced by macroeconomic news. The impact of quantified news sentiment on the price volatility is modelled through a parametrized, non-linear functional map. This approach is motivated by the successful use of a similar model structure in our earlier work, for predicting individual stock volatility using stock-specific news. We claim the proposed model structure for incorporating macroeconomic news together with historical (market) data is novel and improves the accuracy of price prediction quite significantly. We report results of extensive numerical experiments which justify our claim.</jats:p>",

      },
      "abstract": "<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title><jats:p>This paper studies the impact of trading on government bond prices surrounding the release of macroeconomic news. The results show a significant increase in the informational role of trading following economic announcements, which suggests the release of public information increases the level of information asymmetry in the government bond market. The informational role of trading is greater after announcements with a larger initial price impact, and the relation is associated with the surprise component of the announcement and the precision of the public information. The results provide evidence that government bond order flow reveals fundamental information about riskless rates.</jats:p>",

      "abstract": "<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>\n                  <jats:p>We document large average excess returns on U.S. equities in anticipation of monetary policy decisions made at scheduled meetings of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) in the past few decades. These pre‐FOMC returns have increased over time and account for sizable fractions of total annual realized stock returns. While other major international equity indices experienced similar pre‐FOMC returns, we find no such effect in U.S. Treasury securities and money market futures. Other major U.S. macroeconomic news announcements also do not give rise to preannouncement excess equity returns. We discuss challenges in explaining these returns with standard asset pricing theory.</jats:p>",

        ]
      },
      "abstract": "<jats:p>Optimal liquidation using volume weighted average price (VWAP) strategies has been considered in the literature, though never in the presence of permanent market impact and only rarely with execution costs. Moreover, only VWAP strategies have been studied, and the pricing of guaranteed VWAP contracts has never been addressed. In this article, we develop a model to price guaranteed VWAP contracts in a general framework for market impact, and we highlight the differences between an agency VWAP and a guaranteed VWAP contract. Numerical methods and applications are also provided.</jats:p>",

      "short-container-title": [
        "Financ Innov"
      ],
      "abstract": "<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>This study examines the volatility spillovers in four representative exchanges and for six liquid cryptocurrencies. Using the high-frequency trading data of exchanges, the heterogeneity of exchanges in terms of volatility spillover can be examined dynamically in the time and frequency domains. We find that Ripple is a net receiver on Coinbase but acts as a net contributor on other exchanges. Bitfinex and Binance have different net spillover effects on the six cryptocurrency markets. Finally, we identify the determinants of total connectedness in two types of volatility spillover, which can explain cryptocurrency or exchange interlinkage.</jats:p>",

      "abstract": "<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>\n          <jats:p>This study investigates how the uncertainty surrounding cryptocurrency affects cryptocurrency returns (CR) by employing various wavelet techniques. We concentrate on the recently published cryptocurrency uncertainty index (UCRY) and the top eight cryptocurrencies by market capitalization from December 30, 2013, to June 30, 2023. Our results showed that the UCRY index strongly predicted CR. In particular, the UCRY index has a leading position at all frequencies for all cryptocurrencies in our sample. Additionally, when the impacts of economic policy uncertainty and the volatility index are eliminated, the significant comovement of UCRY-CR remains unchanged for the short-, medium-, and long-term investment horizons. Therefore, we conclude that the UCRY-CR relationship is both persistent and pervasive. Our study contributes toward the literature on the relationships between cryptocurrencies and market uncertainties, as well as toward investors who use uncertainty indices to design investment strategies for their portfolios.</jats:p>",

      "abstract": "<jats:p>As an emerging digital asset, Bitcoin has been traded for more than a decade, reaching an impressively high market capitalization and continuing to expand its volume of trading at a rapid pace. Many countries have legalized or are considering legalizing a trading platform for this asset, and a set of companies worldwide accept it as a medium of exchange. As a result of this expansion, many studies in finance literature have focused on studying the efficiency of this cryptocurrency. In line with this literature, this paper investigates, using the abnormal returns and abnormal trading volumes methodologies, the dynamics of investors’ reaction to the arrival of unexpected favorable and unfavorable information regarding the Bitcoin market in the context of the three famous hypotheses: the overreaction, the uncertain information, and the efficient market hypotheses. Overall, we find evidence confirming that the Bitcoin market tends to mature over time. More precisely, over the entire analyzed period, investors behave in accordance with the predictions of the uncertain information hypothesis when positive and negative events occur. However, splitting the timespan into sub-periods provides interesting insights. Remarkably in this respect is the fact that starting with the second sub-period, the response of investors in the Bitcoin market supports, in a moderate manner, the postulate of the efficient market hypothesis when favorable events are addressed. Moreover, our findings reveal that during the pandemic period, the efficiency of Bitcoin has increased, thus turning this stressful period into an advantage for this cryptocurrency. This improved market efficiency is also supported by the abnormal trading volume analysis.</jats:p>",

      "abstract": "<jats:p>A significant correlation between financial news with stock market trends has been explored extensively. However, very little research has been conducted for stock prediction models that utilize news categories, weighted according to their relevance with the target stock. In this paper, we show that prediction accuracy can be enhanced by incorporating weighted news categories simultaneously into the prediction model. We suggest utilizing news categories associated with the structural hierarchy of the stock market: that is, news categories for the market, sector, and stock-related news. In this context, Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) based Weighted and Categorized News Stock prediction model (WCN-LSTM) is proposed. The model incorporates news categories with their learned weights simultaneously. To enhance the effectiveness, sophisticated features are integrated into WCN-LSTM. These include, hybrid input, lexicon-based sentiment analysis, and deep learning to impose sequential learning. Experiments have been performed for the case of the Pakistan Stock Exchange (PSX) using different sentiment dictionaries and time steps. Accuracy and F1-score are used to evaluate the prediction model. We have analyzed the WCN-LSTM results thoroughly and identified that WCN-LSTM performs better than the baseline model. Moreover, the sentiment lexicon HIV4 along with time steps 3 and 7, optimized the prediction accuracy. We have conducted statistical analysis to quantitatively assess our findings. A qualitative comparison of WCN-LSTM with existing prediction models is also presented to highlight its superiority and novelty over its counterparts.</jats:p>",

      "short-container-title": [],
      "abstract": "<jats:p>This paper investigates the link between Bitcoin and macroeconomic fundamentals by estimating the impact of macroeconomic news on Bitcoin using an event study with intraday data. The key result is that, unlike other U.S. asset classes, Bitcoin is orthogonal to monetary and macroeconomic news. This disconnect is puzzling as unexpected changes in discount rates should, in principle, affect the price of Bitcoin even when interpreting Bitcoin as a purely speculative asset.</jats:p>",

      "short-container-title": [],
      "abstract": "<jats:p>Layering and spoofing are among the fastest growing market manipulation techniques, involving placing non-genuine orders into a market to deceive other traders. We develop empirical techniques to detect this prohibited trading. Using a comprehensive, global sample of prosecuted cases and out-of-sample cross-validation tests, we find that the best empirical indicators of spoofing include unbalanced order book quotes, high order activity, abnormal order cancellations, as well as cyclical patterns in market depth and cancellations. Models combining these characteristics achieve high out-of-sample detection accuracy rates, especially when combined with machine learning.</jats:p>",
      "DOI": "10.2139/ssrn.4525036",

  {
    "file": "BASE_PAPER_MASTER_CLASSNOTES.md",
    "line": 18,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "5. [The Mathematics of Cross-Attention (Plain English + Equations)](#5-the-mathematics-of-cross-attention-plain-english--equations)"
  },
  {
    "file": "BASE_PAPER_MASTER_CLASSNOTES.md",
    "line": 95,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "│                  2. THE CROSS-ATTENTION CORE                  │"
  },
  {
    "file": "BASE_PAPER_MASTER_CLASSNOTES.md",
    "line": 101,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "│   Cross-Attention calculates similarity:                      │"
  },
  {
    "file": "BASE_PAPER_MASTER_CLASSNOTES.md",
    "line": 115,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "## 5. The Mathematics of Cross-Attention (Plain English + Equations)"
  },
  {
    "file": "BASE_PAPER_MASTER_CLASSNOTES.md",
    "line": 119,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "In X-Trend, the authors use **Cross-Attention**: the current market looks across at a completely *different* set of historical data."
  },
  {
    "file": "BASE_PAPER_MASTER_CLASSNOTES.md",
    "line": 162,
    "categories": [
      "novelty",
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "To prove this wasn't just curve-fitted luck on one stock, the Oxford team ran a massive, institutional-scale backtest:"
  },
  {
    "file": "BASE_PAPER_MASTER_CLASSNOTES.md",
    "line": 170,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "  3. *Static Neural Forecasters:* Standard Transformer models without few-shot cross-attention."
  },
  {
    "file": "BASE_PAPER_MASTER_CLASSNOTES.md",
    "line": 194,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "3. **Cross-Attention Output:** Shape `[32, 21, Hidden_Dim]`"
  },
  {
    "file": "BASE_PAPER_MASTER_CLASSNOTES.md",
    "line": 203,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "To publish a Q1 paper of our own, we must identify what Oxford left unsolved. Wood et al. has **three massive, glaring limitations**:"
  },
  {
    "file": "BASE_PAPER_MASTER_CLASSNOTES.md",
    "line": 227,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "- **What is the core mechanism?** Slicing history into regime blocks via Change-Point Detection, storing them in a Context Set, and using Transformer Cross-Attention to match today's market to historical crash analogues."
  },
  {
    "file": "BINANCE_DATA_AND_BASE_PAPER.md",
    "line": 24,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "- **Description:** Institutional and retail positioning indicators published daily:"
  },
  {
    "file": "BINANCE_DATA_AND_BASE_PAPER.md",
    "line": 26,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "  - `top_trader_long_short_ratio` (Accounts & Positions): Ratio of long vs. short positions held by elite institutional accounts."
  },
  {
    "file": "BINANCE_DATA_AND_BASE_PAPER.md",
    "line": 29,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "- **Project Role:** **Critical Environmental Filter.** Distinguishes between high-conviction institutional breakouts (price rising + OI expanding + elite trader long ratio high) and fake retail breakouts (price rising into resistance + retail heavily long + OI declining / short covering)."
  },
  {
    "file": "BINANCE_DATA_AND_BASE_PAPER.md",
    "line": 35,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "### 4. `bookTicker` (Top of Book Best Bid & Ask)"
  },
  {
    "file": "BINANCE_DATA_AND_BASE_PAPER.md",
    "line": 47,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "### 7. `trades` & `bookDepth`"
  },
  {
    "file": "BINANCE_DATA_AND_BASE_PAPER.md",
    "line": 76,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "- **Upper Barrier (TP):** $P_t + (2 \\times \\sigma_t)$ for long ($P_t - 2\\sigma_t$ for short)"
  },
  {
    "file": "DATASET_COLLECTION_SPECIFICATION.md",
    "line": 14,
    "categories": [
      "novelty",
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "To train our Few-Shot Metric Network and ensure our empirical evaluation survives Q1 peer review, our dataset must integrate three distinct, synchronized data streams with **zero lookahead bias**:"
  },
  {
    "file": "DATASET_COLLECTION_SPECIFICATION.md",
    "line": 28,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "│ • Role: Identifies institutional vs. retail leverage imbalances        │"
  },
  {
    "file": "DATASET_COLLECTION_SPECIFICATION.md",
    "line": 31,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "│ • Source: High-impact release schedule (1,030+ events 2021-2026)       │"
  },
  {
    "file": "DATASET_COLLECTION_SPECIFICATION.md",
    "line": 32,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "│ • Granularity: Minute-level timestamps + Surprise Z-scores             │"
  },
  {
    "file": "DATASET_COLLECTION_SPECIFICATION.md",
    "line": 44,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "- **Total Candle Count:** $\\approx 184,000$ consecutive 15-minute candles."
  },
  {
    "file": "DATASET_COLLECTION_SPECIFICATION.md",
    "line": 50,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "2. `open`: First fill price of the 15m bar."

    "line": 41,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "  - **Null Hypothesis ($H_0$):** Conditioning an ATR-based trend heuristic on few-shot order-flow prototypes and macroeconomic countdown clocks yields an out-of-sample Sharpe ratio and profit factor statistically indistinguishable from the un-filtered indicator baseline ($\\Delta \\text{Sharpe} \\le 0, p \\ge 0.05$)."
  },
  {
    "file": "MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md",
    "line": 42,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "  - **Alternative Hypothesis ($H_1$):** Few-shot trajectory conditioning produces a statistically significant out-of-sample performance improvement ($\\Delta \\text{Sharpe} > 0, p < 0.01$) after deducting exchange fees and slippage, reducing peak-to-trough drawdown by $\\ge 40\\%$."

  {
    "file": "MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md",
    "line": 49,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "- **The Failure Mode:** When an abrupt regime shock occurs (e.g., COVID-19 March 2020 crash, FTX collapse, emergency rate hikes), static weights $\\theta^*$ optimized for pre-crash drift continue taking losing trades. X-Trend (Wood et al., 2024) proves that few-shot context conditioning adapts in $<5$ bars without slow gradient retraining."
  },
  {
    "file": "MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md",
    "line": 67,
    "categories": [

    ],
    "text": "- Evaluates whether the candidate breakout is trading at an institutional premium or discount:"

  {

    "line": 94,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "### 3.3 Microstructure Spoofing & Manipulation Defense"

    "line": 96,
    "categories": [

    "text": "- **Why We Are Immune to Spoofing:** Resting limit order walls (Level 2 DOM) can be canceled for free. Executed Taker Delta requires paying real exchange fees and crossing the spread. Our model trains strictly on executed taker volume."

    "categories": [

    "categories": [

    ],
    "text": "### 4.2 Standardized Macro Surprise Score ($Z$)"

    "file": "MASTER_METHODOLOGY_REVISION_DOSSIER.md",
    "line": 117,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "  where $A$ is Actual, $F$ is Consensus Forecast, and $\\sigma$ is the historical standard deviation of surprises for indicator $i$."

    "line": 125,
    "categories": [
      "novelty",
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "  Proves econometric causality by testing whether return variance $\\sigma_{\\text{event}}^2 > 3.0 \\times \\sigma_{\\text{normal}}^2$ at $p < 0.001$ during $[-5\\text{m}, +15\\text{m}]$ release windows."

    "line": 132,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "- Fama (1970) and Lo & MacKinlay (1988): Predicting exact candle wicks point-by-point compounds Brownian noise ($O(\\sigma \\sqrt{t})$). We formulate the problem as **Path Signature / Trajectory Classification**."
  },

    ],

  {

    "line": 186,
    "categories": [

    ],
    "text": "$$\\text{If } \\min_k d_k(\\mathbf{x}_q) > \\tau_{\\text{novelty}} \\quad \\text{OR} \\quad P(y = 0 \\mid \\mathbf{x}_q) \\ge 0.40 \\implies \\mathbf{ABSTAIN}$$"

    "categories": [

    ],
    "text": "### 8.1 Combinatorial Purged Cross-Validation (CPCV)"

  {
    "file": "Q1_PEER_REVIEW_REJECTION_AUDIT.md",
    "line": 1,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "# Q1 Peer Review Rejection Audit & Scientific Novelty Defense"
  },
  {
    "file": "Q1_PEER_REVIEW_REJECTION_AUDIT.md",
    "line": 3,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "**Document Identifier:** AUDIT-Q1-BTC-REJECTION-2026-V1  "
  },
  {
    "file": "Q1_PEER_REVIEW_REJECTION_AUDIT.md",
    "line": 18,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "> *\"The authors present an engineering assembly of known parts: Wood et al.'s X-Trend model + an off-the-shelf retail technical indicator (Chandelier Exit) + Binance volume delta + a public economic calendar. There is no new neural network architecture, no new loss derivation, and no new econometric theorem. This is applied software engineering, suitable for an industry blog or trading desk writeup, but lacks the theoretical novelty required for a Q1 journal.\"*"
  },
  {
    "file": "Q1_PEER_REVIEW_REJECTION_AUDIT.md",
    "line": 28,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "> *\"The authors propose calculating macroeconomic surprise scores ($Z = (A - F)/\\sigma$). However, initial release figures are frequently subject to post-release revisions. If the authors used revised historical data rather than point-in-time real-time releases, the model suffers from lookahead leakage. Furthermore, did the authors account for funding rate payments every 8 hours and exchange maintenance disconnects?\"*"
  },
  {
    "file": "Q1_PEER_REVIEW_REJECTION_AUDIT.md",
    "line": 31,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "> *\"Financial returns on 15m crypto have a signal-to-noise ratio below 2%. What evidence proves that the complex cross-attentive few-shot metric network justifies its parameter overhead? Does it meaningfully outperform a simple L1-regularized logistic regression or a rule-based trend filter after fees? If an ablation shows linear models perform comparably, the few-shot architecture is over-engineering financial noise.\"*"
  },
  {
    "file": "Q1_PEER_REVIEW_REJECTION_AUDIT.md",
    "line": 35,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "## Part 2: Why This CAN Be a Q1 Paper — What Scientific Novelty ACTUALLY Means"
  },
  {
    "file": "Q1_PEER_REVIEW_REJECTION_AUDIT.md",
    "line": 37,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "The reason you asked *\"why do you think this will be a Q1? I'm not inventing anything actually here\"* is because you have the common misconception that **Q1 papers must invent a brand-new neural network from scratch (like inventing the Transformer).**"
  },
  {
    "file": "Q1_PEER_REVIEW_REJECTION_AUDIT.md",
    "line": 48,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "│ 2. New Benchmark /      │ The FIRST rigorous measurement of an         │"
  },
  {
    "file": "Q1_PEER_REVIEW_REJECTION_AUDIT.md",
    "line": 59,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "### What OUR Genuine Q1 Contribution Actually Is:"
  },
  {
    "file": "Q1_PEER_REVIEW_REJECTION_AUDIT.md",
    "line": 66,
    "categories": [
      "novelty",
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "   We prove that macroscopic few-shot regime adaptation models (like Oxford's X-Trend) **break down completely on intraday time series unless grounded in centralized taker order flow and deterministic macroeconomic clocks**. We demonstrate the exact mathematical mechanism: price-only attention matrices confuse retail liquidity sweeps with institutional breakouts."
  },
  {
    "file": "Q1_PEER_REVIEW_REJECTION_AUDIT.md",
    "line": 68,
    "categories": [
      "novelty",
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "   We reformulate the mathematically intractable problem of multi-step candlestick point prediction into **Few-Shot Trajectory Archetype Classification**, establishing the first formal path-signature benchmark comparing metric few-shot spaces against standard static GBDTs."
  },
  {
    "file": "Q1_PEER_REVIEW_REJECTION_AUDIT.md",
    "line": 70,
    "categories": [
      "novelty",
      "microstructure",
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "   We provide the first fee-adjusted, Combinatorial Purged Cross-Validation (CPCV) benchmark of retail ATR trailing exits on cryptocurrency derivatives, establishing baseline empirical boundaries under institutional fee drag."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 20,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "2. **Tier 2 (The Institutional AI Gatekeeper):** Instead of executing every signal blindly, an advanced **Few-Shot Metric Learning Model** (pioneered by quantitative researchers at the University of Oxford) inspects what institutional traders are actually doing at that exact millisecond. It analyzes **centralized order flow** (who is aggressively buying vs. selling) and a **macroeconomic countdown clock** (minutes remaining until major news releases like CPI, NFP, or FOMC)."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 22,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "   - **Path 1: Clean Impulse Expansion:** Strong institutional backing $\\to$ Execute immediately at market with a strict **2:1 Risk-to-Reward ratio** (aiming for $+2\\times$ volatility profit target, risking $-1\\times$ volatility stop loss)."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 81,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "│   Measures Euclidean distance to 3 Learned Trajectory Prototypes│"
  },
  {

    "line": 87,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": " Institutional Buying      Retail Stop Hunt       Chop / News Collision"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 102,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "- **The Underlying Market Mechanism:** Large institutional market participants are actively sweeping the order book (high positive Taker Buy Delta). The breakout is backed by real capital."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 105,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "### Archetype 2: Deep Liquidity Sweep / Retest (The Smart Money Re-Entry)"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 117,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "## 4. The Data Engine: 100% Free, Institutional-Grade Data"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 119,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "A key operational strength of this project is that **we do not need to spend thousands of dollars on expensive institutional data feeds** (like Bloomberg, CME DataMine, or RavenPack). We assemble a world-class research dataset using verified, free public repositories:"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 145,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "## 5. Academic Foundations & Q1 Publication Strategy"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 151,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "- **Institutional Heritage:** Oxford-Man Institute of Quantitative Finance, Department of Engineering Science, University of Oxford."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 152,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "- **What Wood et al. Proved:** Systematic trend-following strategies fail during abrupt market regime changes because traditional models adapt too slowly. Few-shot metric learning allows a trading strategy to adapt to new market regimes using only a handful ($K=3\\text{ to }5$) of recent examples."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 154,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "### 5.2 Our Novel Q1 Scientific Contributions (Why This Paper Gets Accepted)"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 155,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "In academic peer review, simply running an existing algorithm on a new dataset is rejected as an \"incremental application\" (Q2 quality). To guarantee a **Q1 publication** in *The Journal of Financial Data Science* or *Quantitative Finance*, we introduce three distinct theoretical contributions that solve the explicitly stated limitations of the Oxford paper:"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 158,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "2. **Point-in-Time Macroeconomic Conditioning:** We prove that financial metric spaces warp significantly prior to scheduled macroeconomic events. Incorporating a deterministic countdown clock (`minutes_to_news`) provides an automated mathematical risk-abstention mechanism."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 170,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "  *(At 2:1 R:R, the mathematical break-even win rate is $33.4\\%$. A $45\\%$ win rate yields an institutional-grade expected return of $+0.35R$ per signal).*"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 172,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "  *(Engineered specifically to pass institutional and prop-firm risk management hurdles).*"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 175,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "- **Statistical Significance (Deflated Sharpe Ratio):** $p < 0.01$  "
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 176,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "  *(Corrected for multiple testing bias via Bailey & López de Prado's Deflated Sharpe Ratio test to prove the edge is genuine skill, not data-snooping luck).*"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 190,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "• Build the Prototypical Metric Network in PyTorch"
  },
  {

    "line": 193,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "• Compute Euclidean distances to Class Prototypes (Expansion, Sweep, Collapse)"
  },
  {

    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "• Implement Combinatorial Purged Cross-Validation (CPCV)"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 202,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "• Compute Deflated Sharpe Ratio and Target Shuffling Noise Tests"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 217,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "> We are taking a well-known trend indicator and putting a brilliant AI security guard in front of it. When the indicator says 'Buy', our AI checks two things in under 10 milliseconds: **Are institutional buyers actually backing this move with real volume?** and **Is a major economic news bomb about to drop?** "
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_PROPOSAL.md",
    "line": 219,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "> If the conditions are great, it buys with a 2-to-1 profit target. If it senses a retail stop-hunt, it waits to buy at a discount. If the market is choppy or dangerous, it does nothing. We are turning a losing retail indicator into an institutional trading system backed by Oxford research.\"*"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 31,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "Oxford applied Few-Shot Learning using **Transformer Cross-Attention** (In-Context Pattern Retrieval without gradient weight updates):"
  },
  {

    "line": 72,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "   - Is price trading above the Session VWAP? (Institutional value confirmation)."

  {

    "line": 73,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "   - Is Binance Taker Delta positive? (Aggressive institutional market buying)."
  },
  {

    "categories": [

    ],
    "text": "4. **Few-Shot Metric Matching:** The model projects this vector into our 16-D embedding space and measures Euclidean distance to the 3 class prototypes:"

  {

    "line": 82,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "## Question 2: How Will This Become a High-Impact Q1 Journal Paper?"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 85,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "> *\"How this thing will become a Q1 paper? What makes reviewers accept it in a top-tier journal?\"*"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 89,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "### The Q1 Peer-Review Standard"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 90,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "Top-tier Q1 journals (*The Journal of Financial Data Science*, *Quantitative Finance*, *ACM Transactions on Economics and Computation*) desk-reject 80% of submissions that do **\"Naive Engineering Applications\"** (e.g., *\"We downloaded Bitcoin data and ran an LSTM on it\"*)."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 100,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "- **Our Q1 Contribution:** We solve their exact open problem by proving that **Order Flow Delta (Taker Volume)** and **Point-in-Time News Distance** provide the missing orthogonal information that separates true breakouts from false sweeps in few-shot latent space."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 103,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "Amateur papers publish backtests with zero fees. We enforce institutional standards:"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 104,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "1. **Combinatorial Purged Cross-Validation (CPCV):** Testing across 15 historical paths with zero label leakage."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 105,
    "categories": [
      "novelty",
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "2. **Deflated Sharpe Ratio (DSR):** Applying Bailey & López de Prado's test to prove our edge is not lucky data-snooping ($p < 0.01$)."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 107,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "4. **Target Shuffling Noise Test:** Proving that scrambling the labels destroys the strategy's Sharpe ratio back to 0.0."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 125,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "- **Key Finding:** Proves that few-shot in-context learning outperforms traditional supervised models on stock prediction when annotated training samples are scarce. Shows that providing LLMs with $K$ historical market examples improves directional accuracy by over 14%."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 130,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "- **Key Finding:** Audits 49,799 financial news articles and proves that **over 90% of published news-trading models cheat unintentionally** due to temporal leakage (e.g., attaching article sentiment to candles before the news was actually published). This justifies why our **Point-in-Time News Countdown Clock** (`minutes_to_news`) is scientifically superior to raw scraping."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 141,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "- **Key Finding:** Evaluates combining numerical price features with textual news headlines. Proves that multi-modal models achieve superior regime adaptation compared to models using numerical price action alone."
  },

    "line": 191,
    "categories": [

    ],
    "text": "### Part 1: The Foundational Science (What the Literature Proves)"
  },
  {

    "categories": [

    ],

It is that physical order flow hitting the order book that actually drives price changes!**"

  {

    "line": 213,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "  [INSTITUTIONAL BELIEF DISPERSION]"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 224,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "   - Level 2: $59,950 bid (25 BTC) -> WIPED OUT"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 225,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "   - Level 3: $59,900 bid (50 BTC) -> WIPED OUT"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 234,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "## Question 6: Pre-News Liquidity Magnets, News Attribution Gap, and Order Size Classification (Whales vs. Retail)"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 246,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "   - Above the market: Resting buy-stop orders (retail short stop-losses) and institutional limit sell walls."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 247,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "   - Below the market: Resting sell-stop orders (retail long stop-losses) and institutional limit buy walls."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 248,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "3. **The Pre-News Sweep:** Institutional algorithms frequently drive price into these large order clusters right before the release to fill institutional inventory (a \"liquidity sweep\")."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 269,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "#### 3. The \"Surprise Delta\" (What Actually Moves the Market):"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 270,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "Markets do **not** move because of the raw number. Markets move because of the **SURPRISE**:"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 271,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "$$\\text{Surprise } Z = \\frac{\\text{Actual} - \\text{Forecast}}{\\sigma_{\\text{historical}}}$$"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 272,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "- If CPI is forecast at $3.1\\%$ and comes out at $3.1\\%$, Surprise $Z = 0.0$. Price barely reacts."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 273,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "- If CPI is forecast at $3.1\\%$ and comes out at $3.5\\%$, Surprise $Z = +4.0$ (a 4-sigma shock). Price immediately crashes because the market must re-price unexpected inflation!"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 277,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "### Sub-Problem 3: The Scientific Gap — How Do We PROVE the News Caused the Price Spike?"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 279,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "In academic econometrics, this is known as the **Causality / Identification Problem**. How do we prove mathematically that a 15m candle spike was caused by the news announcement and not by random market noise?"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 295,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "### Sub-Problem 4: Classifying Order Values (Whales vs. Retail)"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 314,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "│ BUCKET 4: WHALES /    │ Size > 10.0 BTC │ Aggressive market sweepers.  │"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 319,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "#### The Golden Metric: \"Whale Delta\" vs. \"Retail Delta\""
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 321,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "$$\\text{Delta}_{\\text{Whale}} = \\text{Taker Buy Vol}_{(>1\\text{ BTC})} - \\text{Taker Sell Vol}_{(>1\\text{ BTC})}$$"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 324,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "- **The Institutional Divergence Rule:**"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 325,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "  - If $\\text{Delta}_{\\text{Retail}} > 0$ (retail is buying the breakout), BUT $\\text{Delta}_{\\text{Whale}} \\ll 0$ (whales are aggressively market-dumping into them):  "
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 327,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "  - If $\\text{Delta}_{\\text{Whale}} \\gg 0$ (whales are aggressively sweeping the ask queues):  "
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 359,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "│   used in TradingView Pine Script and institutional algorithms.        │"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 387,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "   - *Role:* Proves to peer reviewers that ATR volatility exit indicators possess empirical predictive power inside deep neural networks."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 433,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "- If you look **only at News**, you get tricked. Many times \"bullish news\" drops, retail traders buy, but smart money uses that exit liquidity to dump their bags (the car stalls and crashes)."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 450,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "│ 3. [NEWS SURPRISE]    surprise_z: (Actual - Forecast) / StdDev         │"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 453,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "│ 6. [WHALE SIZING]     whale_delta_ratio: Whale Delta / Retail Delta    │"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 465,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "#### Scenario 1: The True Institutional Breakout (Clean Expansion — Archetype 1)"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 466,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "- **The News:** US CPI inflation drops to 2.8% (Forecast was 3.1%). `surprise_z = -3.2` (strongly dovish / bullish for Bitcoin)."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 469,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "- **The Whale Delta:** `whale_delta_ratio = +8.2` (Whales are responsible for 85% of the aggressive buying)."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 470,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "- **What the Model Learns:** When positive news is verified by overwhelming Whale Buy Delta, price almost never retests the entry candle."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 477,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "- **The Order Flow (The Lie Detector):** Retail traders are buying (`retail_delta = +$12M`), BUT Whale Delta is **heavily negative** (`whale_delta = -$45M`)."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 498,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "2. In this 16-D space, the network computes the **Euclidean Distance** to the 3 learned class prototypes:"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 503,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure",
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "   - If the model saw positive news + whale buying and predicted Class 1, and the trade indeed hit +2R $\\to$ The gradient pulls $\\mathbf{z}_t$ closer to prototype $\\mathbf{c}_{\\text{expansion}}$."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 504,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure",
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "   - If the model saw positive news but missed the whale dump, and the trade lost money $\\to$ The gradient violently pushes $\\mathbf{z}_t$ away from the expansion prototype and pulls it into the sweep/collapse prototype!"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 506,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "Over thousands of historical episodes, the neural network learns a geometric map where **Order Flow confirms or denies the News**, giving you an automated institutional filter."

    "text": "#### Path 2: Liquidity Sweep / Retest (The Smart Money Limit Order)"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1522,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "- **Why wait:** The AI detects retail absorption divergence (retail is buying, but Whale Delta is negative). An immediate entry at the candle close will get stopped out by market makers sweeping retail liquidity!"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1544,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "Executing **both** orders simultaneously is a legitimate, widely used institutional execution technique known as **Dual-Tranche Split Execution** (or *Scale-In Execution*)."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1548,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "- *\"If I only use Market Orders, I get chopped up when price sweeps the stop line first!\"*"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1632,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "### 2. Session VWAP (Institutional Fair Value Benchmark)"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1637,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "- **Institutional Rule:**"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1638,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "  - If $\\Delta \\text{VWAP} > 0$: Price is trading at a premium to institutional intraday accumulation."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1650,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "### The Literature-Backed Upgrade: Moving from Retail Indicators to Institutional Value Bands"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1652,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "In real quantitative finance, using raw single lines (like a single VWAP line or raw ATR) is considered naive. Institutional algorithms evaluate **statistical dispersion around value benchmarks**."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1665,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "│ • The Mechanism: Institutional traders don't just look at the VWAP     │"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1668,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure",
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "│   - +2σ Band = Institutional Overbought (Take Profit zone)             │"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1669,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure",
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "│   - -2σ Band = Institutional Oversold (Extreme Discount zone)         │"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1677,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "│   shifts! Proves that when price breaks out beyond the 1σ VWAP band    │"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1687,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "│   Bitcoin, proving that institutional HFT algorithms cluster their     │"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1696,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "#### 1. Preventing \"Top-Buying\" with $+2\\sigma$ VWAP Upper Bands"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1699,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "  If the Chandelier Exit prints a \"BUY\", but price is already extended beyond the **$+2\\sigma$ VWAP Upper Band**, the AI detects that price is statistically overextended relative to the session's volume. **The AI blocks the market order!** It waits for price to pull back to the mean before entering."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1703,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "- **Weekly VWAP (Monday 00:00 UTC):** Defines institutional macro weekly fair value."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1704,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "- **The Institutional Confluence Rule (Petukhina et al., 2020):**  "
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1705,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "  When price is above **BOTH** the Daily VWAP and the Weekly Anchored VWAP, a Chandelier Exit Buy signal has **over $2.4\\times$ higher statistical continuation expectancy** than when it is fighting against the weekly institutional trend!"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1775,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "│ 2. SESSION VWAP +2σ / -2σ VARIANCE BANDS [ADOPT - CRITICAL UPGRADE]    │"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1777,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "│ • Feature: vwap_zscore = (Close - VWAP) / sigma_VWAP in [-3.0, +3.0]   │"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1779,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "│ • Decision Logic: If vwap_zscore > +2.0, DO NOT buy at market; wait    │"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1801,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "2. `vwap_zscore`: How stretched is price relative to session volume? (e.g. $+0.4$ is healthy, $+2.6$ is an overbought trap)."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1802,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "3. `weekly_trend_bias`: `1` if aligned with the weekly institutional anchor, `0` if fighting the macro week."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1804,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "This setup is clean, computationally instantaneous (<0.1ms), avoids indicator clutter, and gives our Few-Shot AI the exact institutional context it needs!"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1822,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "- **Why it is 100% mandatory:** Without Pillar 1, our manuscript is not a research paper—it is just an undocumented script. Every Q1 journal editor requires $H_0$ and $H_1$ by definition."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1833,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "2. **Session VWAP Z-Score (`vwap_zscore`):**  "
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1850,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "2. **`vwap_zscore` $\\in [-3.0, +3.0]$:** Is price sitting at fair value ($\\approx 0.0$) or is it an overextended trap ($> +2.0$)?"

  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1852,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "Everything else (Order Flow Delta, Whales, News Clocks) belongs where it naturally shines: **in Pillars 3 and 4**."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1854,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "This keeps Pillar 2 razor-sharp, zero-bloat, and lightning fast (<0.01ms compute)!"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1858,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "## Question 25: How Reviewer 2 Will Reject This Paper & Why It Still Qualifies as Q1"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1861,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "> *\"Why do you think this will be a Q1? I'm not inventing anything actually here. And tell me how a human will reject this research as a Q1?\"*"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1865,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "### 1. The Core Realization: What Q1 Actually Requires"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1866,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "A common misconception in applied research is that a Q1 manuscript must invent a completely novel deep learning architecture from scratch (e.g. inventing Transformers or GANs). In top quantitative finance and financial data science journals (*Journal of Financial Data Science*, *Quantitative Finance*, *ACM ICAIF*), **that is not how papers are evaluated.**"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1869,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "1. **Methodological Novelty:** Solving a documented failure mode in a SOTA baseline."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1870,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "2. **Empirical Measurement & Benchmarking:** First rigorous, reproducible measurement of an unquantified phenomenon."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1872,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "4. **Systematic Falsification:** Empirically disproving prevailing assumptions under institutional frictions."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1874,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "If written as a retail bot recipe (*\"We combined CE + Binance CVD + News to make money\"*), it will be **instantly desk-rejected**. It achieves Q1 status strictly by framing the work as a **mechanistic solution to the documented limitations of Oxford's X-Trend model (Wood et al., 2024)**."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1882,
    "categories": [
      "model_mechanism"
    ],
    "text": "   - *Our Defense:* Formulate as a rigorous feature ablation study: isolating the exact marginal information coefficient (IC) and cross-attention weight attributed to order-flow microstructure vs price-only history."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1891,
    "categories": [
      "novelty"
    ],
    "text": "   - *Our Defense:* Use unrevised first-release point-in-time figures exclusively, coupled with a pre-announcement countdown clock that uses zero post-release knowledge."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1894,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "   - *Our Defense:* Benchmark against linear models (Logistic, Ridge) and tree ensembles (LightGBM) under Combinatorial Purged Cross-Validation (CPCV). If simpler models match performance, document it honestly (a valuable falsification finding)."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1906,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure",
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "To power our Few-Shot Metric Network and guarantee zero lookahead bias, we collect **three synchronized data streams** from free, public institutional archives:"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1908,
    "categories": [
      "leakage_eval"
    ],
    "text": "1. **Stream 1: Binance USDT-M 15m Klines & Order Flow (2021–2026, ~184,000 Candles):**"
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1916,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],
    "text": "     - Passive Absorption Divergence: Flags when smart money passively absorbs retail breakouts."
  },
  {
    "file": "RESEARCH_QUESTIONS_AND_ANSWERS.md",
    "line": 1917,
    "categories": [
      "microstructure"
    ],

  },
  {

    "line": 1921,
    "categories": [
