Each event <math id=\"S3.p1.m4\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}_{i}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> occurs at a specific timestamp <math id=\"S3.p1.m5\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"i\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">i</annotation></semantics></math> and belongs to one of the event types shown in Table <a href=\"#S2.T1\" title=\"Table 1 ‣ 2.3. Counterfactual Data Augmentation by LLMs ‣ 2. Related Work ‣ CAMEF: Causal-Augmented Multi-Modality Event-Driven Financial Forecasting by Integrating Time Series Patterns and Salient Macroeconomic Announcements\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">1</span></a>A. Each event script <math id=\"S3.p1.m6\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}_{i}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> consists of a sequence of word tokens, represented as <math id=\"S3.p1.m7\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}_{i}:=\\{w_{1},w_{2},\\dots,w_{m}\\}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}_{i}:=\\{w_{1},w_{2},\\dots,w_{m}\\}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S3.p2\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S3.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.p2.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Time Series Data</span> is defined as <math id=\"S3.p2.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{X}:=\\{X_{1},X_{2},\\dots,X_{|\\mathcal{X}|}\\}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒳</mi><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">|</mo><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒳</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\">|</mo></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{X}:=\\{X_{1},X_{2},\\dots,X_{|\\mathcal{X}|}\\}</annotation></semantics></math>, where each <math id=\"S3.p2.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"X_{i}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">X_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> represents the numerical data at time step <math id=\"S3.p2.m3\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"i\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">i</annotation></semantics></math>. An event <math id=\"S3.p2.m4\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}_{i}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> is <span id=\"S3.p2.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">aligned</span> with a time series segment <math id=\"S3.p2.m5\" class=\"ltx_math_unparsed\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{X}_{i-\\tau:i+\\tau}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒳</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo lspace=\"0.278em\" rspace=\"0.278em\">:</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{X}_{i-\\tau:i+\\tau}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id=\"S3.p2.m6\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"i\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">i</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the time of the releasement of the event, and <math id=\"S3.p2.m7\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\tau\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\tau</annotation></semantics></math> represents the duration of the time-series segment both preceding and succeeding time step <math id=\"S3.p2.m8\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"i\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">i</annotation></semantics></math>, denoted as <math id=\"S3.p2.m9\" class=\"ltx_math_unparsed\" alttext=\"[\\mathcal{X}_{i-\\tau:i+\\tau}\\mapsto\\mathcal{E}_{i}]\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">[</mo><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒳</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo lspace=\"0.278em\" rspace=\"0.278em\">:</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\">↦</mo><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\">]</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">[\\mathcal{X}_{i-\\tau:i+\\tau}\\mapsto\\mathcal{E}_{i}]</annotation></semantics></math>. This alignment reflects the time series segment leading up to the event (<math id=\"S3.p2.m10\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{X}_{i-\\tau}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒳</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{X}_{i-\\tau}</annotation></semantics></math>) and the period during which the event is expected to have an effect (<math id=\"S3.p2.m11\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{X}_{i+\\tau}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒳</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{X}_{i+\\tau}</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S3.p3\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S3.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.p3.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Event-Driven Forecasting</span>: Given a dataset <math id=\"S3.p3.m1\" class=\"ltx_math_unparsed\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{U}=\\{[\\mathcal{X}_{i-\\tau:i+\\tau}\\mapsto\\mathcal{E}_{i}]\\}_{i=1}^{n}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒰</mi><mo>=</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">{</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">[</mo><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒳</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo lspace=\"0.278em\" rspace=\"0.278em\">:</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></mrow></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\">↦</mo><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\">]</mo></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{U}=\\{[\\mathcal{X}_{i-\\tau:i+\\tau}\\mapsto\\mathcal{E}_{i}]\\}_{i=1}^{n}</annotation></semantics></math> consisting of <math id=\"S3.p3.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"n\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">n</annotation></semantics></math> aligned event and time-series pairs, for each data pair in <math id=\"S3.p3.m3\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{U}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒰</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{U}</annotation></semantics></math>, the model uses both the event text <math id=\"S3.p3.m4\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}_{i}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and the historical time-series segment <math id=\"S3.p3.m5\" class=\"ltx_math_unparsed\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{X}_{i-\\tau:i}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒳</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>−</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow><mo lspace=\"0.278em\" rspace=\"0.278em\">:</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{X}_{i-\\tau:i}</annotation></semantics></math>, which spans <math id=\"S3.p3.m6\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\tau\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>τ</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\tau</annotation></semantics></math> steps before the event’s release at time <math id=\"S3.p3.m7\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"i\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">i</annotation></semantics></math>, to forecast the future time steps <math id=\"S3.p3.m8\" class=\"ltx_math_unparsed\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{X}_{i+1:i+\\tau}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒳</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo lspace=\"0.278em\" rspace=\"0.278em\">:</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>τ</mi></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{X}_{i+1:i+\\tau}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>\n</div>\n<figure id=\"S3.F2\" class=\"ltx_figure\">\n<div class=\"ltx_flex_figure\">\n<div class=\"ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2\">\n<figure id=\"S3.F2.sf1\" class=\"ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center\"><img src=\"2502.04592v3/figures/scm.drawio.png\" id=\"S3.F2.sf1.g1\" class=\"ltx_graphics ltx_img_square\" style=\"aspect-ratio:476/451;\" width=\"476\" height=\"451\" alt=\"Refer to caption\">\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure\"><span id=\"S3.F2.sf1.3\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">(a)</span> </span><span id=\"S3.F2.sf1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_align_center\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">Causal Effect Graph</span></figcaption>\n</figure></div><div class=\"ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_2\">\n<figure id=\"S3.F2.sf2\" class=\"ltx_figure ltx_figure_panel ltx_align_center\"><img src=\"2502.04592v3/figures/couterfactual.drawio.png\" id=\"S3.F2.sf2.g1\" class=\"ltx_graphics ltx_img_landscape\" style=\"aspect-ratio:476/192;\" width=\"476\" height=\"192\" alt=\"Refer to caption\">\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure\"><span id=\"S3.F2.sf2.3\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">(b)</span> </span><span id=\"S3.F2.sf2.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_align_center\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">Cause-Effect Detection with Counterfactual Events</span></figcaption>\n</figure></div></div>\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption ltx_centering\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure\"><span id=\"S3.F2.3\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">Figure 2</span>. </span><span id=\"S3.F2.4\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">The illustration of causal relationships and counterfactual events.</span></figcaption>\n</figure>\n<div id=\"S3.p4\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S3.p4.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.p4.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Causal Effect Graph:</span> A Causal Effect Graph represents the causal links among variables: textual modality <math id=\"S3.p4.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}</annotation></semantics></math> (event scripts), current price trend <math id=\"S3.p4.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{X}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>, and future time series movements <math id=\"S3.p4.m3\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{Y}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>𝐘</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{Y}</annotation></semantics></math>. In event-driven financial prediction, events influence the market movements of financial assets, forming a causal chain denoted as <math id=\"S3.p4.m4\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}\\rightarrow\\mathcal{X}\\rightarrow\\mathbf{Y}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\">→</mo><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒳</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\">→</mo><mi>𝐘</mi></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}\\rightarrow\\mathcal{X}\\rightarrow\\mathbf{Y}</annotation></semantics></math>, as illustrated in Figure <a href=\"#S3.F2.sf1\" title=\"In Figure 2 ‣ 3. Problem Formulation ‣ CAMEF: Causal-Augmented Multi-Modality Event-Driven Financial Forecasting by Integrating Time Series Patterns and Salient Macroeconomic Announcements\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2(a)</span></a>.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S3.p5\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S3.p5.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S3.p5.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Counterfactual Event:</span> A Counterfactual Event (CE) represents a modified event script in which key variables (e.g., unemployment rates, GDP values) are altered relative to the factual event, while the surrounding context remains unchanged. These events are denoted as <math id=\"S3.p5.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\{\\mathcal{E}^{*}_{1},\\mathcal{E}^{*}_{2},\\ldots,\\mathcal{E}^{*}_{n}\\}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">{</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mn>1</mn><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mn>2</mn><mo>∗</mo></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>n</mi><mo>∗</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\{\\mathcal{E}^{*}_{1},\\mathcal{E}^{*}_{2},\\ldots,\\mathcal{E}^{*}_{n}\\}</annotation></semantics></math>. CEs are utilized to train CAMEF, enabling it to identify factual cause-effect relationships, represented as <math id=\"S3.p5.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}\\rightarrow\\mathcal{X}\\rightarrow\\mathcal{Y}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\">→</mo><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒳</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\">→</mo><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒴</mi></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}\\rightarrow\\mathcal{X}\\rightarrow\\mathcal{Y}</annotation></semantics></math>, as illustrated in Figure <a href=\"#S3.F2.sf2\" title=\"In Figure 2 ‣ 3. Problem Formulation ‣ CAMEF: Causal-Augmented Multi-Modality Event-Driven Financial Forecasting by Integrating Time Series Patterns and Salient Macroeconomic Announcements\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">2(b)</span></a>.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S4\" class=\"ltx_section\">\n<h2 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_section\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_section\">4. </span>Data Collection and Counterfactual Event Augmentation</h2>\n\n<div id=\"S4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">This section introduces the proposed dataset and the methodology for counterfactual event augmentation. The dataset includes 6 types of key macroeconomic announcements ranging from 2004 to 2024, selected through an extensive review of the financial literature, along with _high-frequency trading data. Unlike the daily-based trading data used in previous studies, this high-frequency data provides more predictive accuracy and better reflects real trading behavior in the industry.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S4.SS1\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">4.1. </span>Dataset Acquisition</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S4.SS1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S4.SS1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The primary question guiding the collection of this dataset is: <span id=\"S4.SS1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">“Which macroeconomic releases have the greatest impact on financial markets?”</span> To address this, we conducted a comprehensive review of the financial literature to identify key macroeconomic factors that influence market behavior. Several dominant factors emerged, including the <span id=\"S4.SS1.p1.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">FOMC Minutes</span> <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep\">(<a href=\"#bib.bib11\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">CIESLAK et al., 2019</a>; <a href=\"#bib.bib18\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Gertler and Horvath, 2018</a>; <a href=\"#bib.bib35\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Masciandaro et al., 2024</a>; <a href=\"#bib.bib45\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Rosa, 2016</a>; <a href=\"#bib.bib53\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Tadle, 2022</a>; <a href=\"#bib.bib44\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Rosa, 2013</a>; <a href=\"#bib.bib34\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">LUCCA and MOENCH, 2015</a>; <a href=\"#bib.bib43\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Rosa, 2011</a>)</cite>, along with <span id=\"S4.SS1.p1.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Unemployment Insurance Claims</span>, <span id=\"S4.SS1.p1.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Employment Situation Reports</span>, <span id=\"S4.SS1.p1.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">GDP Advance Releases</span>, and the <span id=\"S4.SS1.p1.1.6\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Consumer Price Index (CPI)</span> and <span id=\"S4.SS1.p1.1.7\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Producer Price Index (PPI)</span> reports <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep\">(<a href=\"#bib.bib39\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Pearce and Roley, 1984</a>; <a href=\"#bib.bib19\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Gilbert et al., 2010</a>; <a href=\"#bib.bib20\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Gilbert et al., 2017</a>; <a href=\"#bib.bib4\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Bartolini et al., 2008</a>; <a href=\"#bib.bib27\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Kim et al., 2004</a>; <a href=\"#bib.bib21\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Goldberg and Grisse, 2013</a>)</cite>, which serve as the textual modality data for our dataset.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S4.SS1.p2\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S4.SS1.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">To collect these data, we developed web crawlers to extract raw files directly from official sources, including HTML, PDF, and TXT formats. These raw files were then pre-processed and converted into a structured and unified text format, ensuring consistency and ease of subsequent analysis. Table <a href=\"#S2.T1\" title=\"Table 1 ‣ 2.3. Counterfactual Data Augmentation by LLMs ‣ 2. Related Work ‣ CAMEF: Causal-Augmented Multi-Modality Event-Driven Financial Forecasting by Integrating Time Series Patterns and Salient Macroeconomic Announcements\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">1</span></a> provides a summary of the data types, collection frequencies, time periods, and sources of the events included in our dataset. Further details on the data crawling and pre-processing methodologies can be found in Appendix B.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S4.SS1.p3\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S4.SS1.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">In addition to the textual data, studies <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep\">(<a href=\"#bib.bib11\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">CIESLAK et al., 2019</a>; <a href=\"#bib.bib18\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Gertler and Horvath, 2018</a>; <a href=\"#bib.bib35\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Masciandaro et al., 2024</a>; <a href=\"#bib.bib45\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Rosa, 2016</a>; <a href=\"#bib.bib53\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Tadle, 2022</a>; <a href=\"#bib.bib44\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Rosa, 2013</a>; <a href=\"#bib.bib34\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">LUCCA and MOENCH, 2015</a>; <a href=\"#bib.bib43\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Rosa, 2011</a>)</cite> have demonstrated that the largest market impacts are typically observed in major U.S. stock indexes and Treasury bonds. Therefore, we focused on collecting high-frequency trading time-series data at 5 minute interval for key stock indexes, including the <span id=\"S4.SS1.p3.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">S&amp;P 500 (SPX)</span>, <span id=\"S4.SS1.p3.1.2\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Dow Industrial (INDU)</span>, <span id=\"S4.SS1.p3.1.3\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">NASDAQ (NDX)</span>, as well as <span id=\"S4.SS1.p3.1.4\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">U.S. Treasury Bond at 1-Month (USGG1M)</span> and <span id=\"S4.SS1.p3.1.5\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Treasury Bond at 5-Year (USGG5YR)</span>.</p>\n</div>\n<figure id=\"S4.F3\" class=\"ltx_figure\"><img src=\"2502.04592v3/figures/Model_Pipeline.drawio.png\" id=\"S4.F3.g1\" class=\"ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape\" style=\"aspect-ratio:476/167;\" width=\"476\" height=\"167\" alt=\"Refer to caption\">\n<figcaption class=\"ltx_caption ltx_centering\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure\"><span id=\"S4.F3.3\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">Figure 3</span>. </span><span id=\"S4.F3.4\" class=\"ltx_text\" style=\"font-size:90%;\">The Pipeline and Neural Architecture of CAMEF</span></figcaption>\n</figure>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S4.SS2\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">4.2. </span>Counterfactual Events Generation based on LLM</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S4.SS2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S4.SS2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">This section describes the process of counterfactual event generation, creating hypothetical scenarios from existing event scripts. The aim is to reflect a target sentiment of a given event script while maintaining logical consistency and coherence of the original script. Our goal is modifying sentiment-relevant elements (such as key facts, sentiment-indicative phrases, or numerical values) without disrupting the sentiment-neutral components of the script.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S4.SS2.p2\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S4.SS2.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Formally, for a given event script <math id=\"S4.SS2.p2.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}_{i}:=\\{w_{1},w_{2},\\dots,w_{m}\\}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}_{i}:=\\{w_{1},w_{2},\\dots,w_{m}\\}</annotation></semantics></math>, the objective is to produce a counterfactual version <math id=\"S4.SS2.p2.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\prime}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msubsup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> that embodies the desired target sentiment <math id=\"S4.SS2.p2.m3\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"S_{i}^{\\prime}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msubsup><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">S_{i}^{\\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>. Conceptually, the event script can be viewed as comprising sentiment-relevant content (<math id=\"S4.SS2.p2.m4\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{sentiment}}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msubsup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi><mtext>sentiment</mtext></msubsup><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{sentiment}}</annotation></semantics></math>) and sentiment-neutral content (<math id=\"S4.SS2.p2.m5\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{neutral}}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msubsup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi><mtext>neutral</mtext></msubsup><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{neutral}}</annotation></semantics></math>), so that <math id=\"S4.SS2.p2.m6\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}_{i}=\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{neutral}}\\cup\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{sentiment}}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi><mtext>neutral</mtext></msubsup><mo>∪</mo><msubsup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi><mtext>sentiment</mtext></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}_{i}=\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{neutral}}\\cup\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{sentiment}}</annotation></semantics></math>. Instead of explicitly decomposing the script, we guide a language model (LLM) using structured prompts to modify only the sentiment-relevant content. This ensures that neutral content remains intact or is replaced with semantically equivalent expressions. Formally:</p>\n<table id=\"S4.E1\" class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table\">\n\n<tbody><tr class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline\">\n<td rowspan=\"1\" class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left\">(1)</span></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft\"></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center\"><math id=\"S4.E1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\prime}=\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{neutral}}\\cup f_{\\text{LLM}}(\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{sentiment}}\\mid S_{i}^{\\prime}),\" display=\"block\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi><mtext>neutral</mtext></msubsup><mo>∪</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext>LLM</mtext></msub><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><msubsup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi><mtext>sentiment</mtext></msubsup><mo fence=\"true\" lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">∣</mo><msubsup><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\prime}=\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{neutral}}\\cup f_{\\text{LLM}}(\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{sentiment}}\\mid S_{i}^{\\prime}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright\"></td></tr></tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S4.SS2.p3\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S4.SS2.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">where <math id=\"S4.SS2.p3.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"f_{\\text{LLM}}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext>LLM</mtext></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">f_{\\text{LLM}}</annotation></semantics></math> adjusts <math id=\"S4.SS2.p3.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{sentiment}}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msubsup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi><mtext>sentiment</mtext></msubsup><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{sentiment}}</annotation></semantics></math> to align with <math id=\"S4.SS2.p3.m3\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"S_{i}^{\\prime}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msubsup><mi>S</mi><mi>i</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">S_{i}^{\\prime}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id=\"S4.SS2.p3.m4\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{neutral}}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msubsup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi><mtext>neutral</mtext></msubsup><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{neutral}}</annotation></semantics></math> remains unchanged or is replaced by equivalent expressions.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S4.SS2.p4\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S4.SS2.p4.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Specifically, we used the LLaMA-3 8B model with a series of carefully designed prompts. These prompts include three key steps, with detailed templates provided in Appendix A:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S4.SS2.p5\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<ol id=\"S4.I1\" class=\"ltx_enumerate\">\n<li id=\"S4.I1.i1\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">(1)</span> \n<div id=\"S4.I1.i1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S4.I1.i1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S4.I1.i1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Summarization Prompt (Appendix A.1):</span> Condenses lengthy event scripts into concise summaries, addressing memory constraints while retaining sentiment-relevant content and key numerical variables.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S4.I1.i2\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">(2)</span> \n<div id=\"S4.I1.i2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S4.I1.i2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S4.I1.i2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Sentiment Analysis Prompt (Appendix A.2):</span> Assigns a sentiment score (from 1, very negative, to 10, very positive) to the original event script. This score provides a baseline for generating counterfactual versions.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S4.I1.i3\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">(3)</span> \n<div id=\"S4.I1.i3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S4.I1.i3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S4.I1.i3.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Counterfactual Generation Prompt (Appendix A.3):</span> Produces multiple counterfactual scripts, each reflecting a different sentiment level. The prompt modifies sentiment-related phrases and numerical values (<math id=\"S4.I1.i3.p1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{sentiment}}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msubsup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi><mtext>sentiment</mtext></msubsup><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{sentiment}}</annotation></semantics></math>) while preserving or equivalently substituting neutral content (<math id=\"S4.I1.i3.p1.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{neutral}}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msubsup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mi>i</mi><mtext>neutral</mtext></msubsup><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}_{i}^{\\text{neutral}}</annotation></semantics></math>). This approach ensures numerical reasonability, sentiment relevance, and structural consistency.</p>\n</div></li>\n</ol>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S4.SS2.p6\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S4.SS2.p6.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">This multi-step prompt strategy facilitates the generation of coherent, contextually relevant counterfactual events, enabling exploration of diverse market scenarios and deeper causal understanding.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S5\" class=\"ltx_section\">\n<h2 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_section\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_section\">5. </span>CAMEF Architecture</h2>\n\n<div id=\"S5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The CAMEF model integrates both textual and time-series information through a structured architecture consisting of a textual encoder, a time-series encoder, and a forecasting decoder, as depicted in Fig. <a href=\"#S4.F3\" title=\"Figure 3 ‣ 4.1. Dataset Acquisition ‣ 4. Data Collection and Counterfactual Event Augmentation ‣ CAMEF: Causal-Augmented Multi-Modality Event-Driven Financial Forecasting by Integrating Time Series Patterns and Salient Macroeconomic Announcements\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">3</span></a>. Each component is detailed below.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S5.SS1\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">5.1. </span>Textual Modality Encoder (<math id=\"S5.SS1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\textbf{CAMEF}_{\\text{Textual}}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msub><mtext class=\"ltx_mathvariant_bold\">CAMEF</mtext><mtext>Textual</mtext></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\textbf{CAMEF}_{\\text{Textual}}</annotation></semantics></math>)</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S5.SS1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">We encode event scripts using RoBERTa <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep\">(<a href=\"#bib.bib32\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Liu et al., 2019</a>)</cite>. Given an input script <math id=\"S5.SS1.p1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{E}_{i}={w_{1},w_{2},\\dots,w_{m}}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐄</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{E}_{i}={w_{1},w_{2},\\dots,w_{m}}</annotation></semantics></math>, RoBERTa produces contextual token embeddings:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS1.p2\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<table id=\"S5.E2\" class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table\">\n\n<tbody><tr class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline\">\n<td rowspan=\"1\" class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left\">(2)</span></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft\"></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center\"><math id=\"S5.E2.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\{\\mathbf{h}_{1},\\mathbf{h}_{2},\\dots,\\mathbf{h}_{m}\\}=\\text{RoBERTa}(\\{w_{1},w_{2},\\dots,w_{m}\\}),\" display=\"block\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">}</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>RoBERTa</mtext><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>m</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\{\\mathbf{h}_{1},\\mathbf{h}_{2},\\dots,\\mathbf{h}_{m}\\}=\\text{RoBERTa}(\\{w_{1},w_{2},\\dots,w_{m}\\}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright\"></td></tr></tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS1.p3\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS1.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">where <math id=\"S5.SS1.p3.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{h}_{j}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{1\\times 768}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace=\"0.222em\" rspace=\"0.222em\">×</mo><mn>768</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{h}_{j}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{1\\times 768}</annotation></semantics></math> is the embedding of token <math id=\"S5.SS1.p3.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"w_{j}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">w_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>. Each embedding is passed through a projection network with three linear layers and GELU activations:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS1.p4\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<table id=\"S5.E3\" class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table\">\n\n<tbody><tr class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline\">\n<td rowspan=\"1\" class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left\">(3)</span></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft\"></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center\"><math id=\"S5.E3.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{e}_{j}=\\mathbf{W}^{(3)}\\cdot\\text{GELU}(\\mathbf{W}^{(2)}\\cdot\\text{GELU}(\\mathbf{W}^{(1)}\\mathbf{h}_{j}+\\mathbf{b}^{(1)})+\\mathbf{b}^{(2)})+\\mathbf{b}^{(3)},\" display=\"block\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace=\"0.222em\" rspace=\"0.222em\">⋅</mo><mtext>GELU</mtext></mrow><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace=\"0.222em\" rspace=\"0.222em\">⋅</mo><mtext>GELU</mtext></mrow><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><msub><mi>𝐡</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>𝐛</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>𝐛</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>𝐛</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{e}_{j}=\\mathbf{W}^{(3)}\\cdot\\text{GELU}(\\mathbf{W}^{(2)}\\cdot\\text{GELU}(\\mathbf{W}^{(1)}\\mathbf{h}_{j}+\\mathbf{b}^{(1)})+\\mathbf{b}^{(2)})+\\mathbf{b}^{(3)},</annotation></semantics></math></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright\"></td></tr></tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS1.p5\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS1.p5.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">where <math id=\"S5.SS1.p5.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{W}^{(1)}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{768\\times 1024}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mn>768</mn><mo lspace=\"0.222em\" rspace=\"0.222em\">×</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{W}^{(1)}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{768\\times 1024}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id=\"S5.SS1.p5.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{W}^{(2)}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{1024\\times 1024}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mn>1024</mn><mo lspace=\"0.222em\" rspace=\"0.222em\">×</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{W}^{(2)}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{1024\\times 1024}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id=\"S5.SS1.p5.m3\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{W}^{(3)}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{1024\\times 768}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mn>1024</mn><mo lspace=\"0.222em\" rspace=\"0.222em\">×</mo><mn>768</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{W}^{(3)}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{1024\\times 768}</annotation></semantics></math>. The final encoding vector <math id=\"S5.SS1.p5.m4\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{E}_{i}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐄</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{E}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> for the script is computed as the average of the transformed embeddings,\n<math id=\"S5.SS1.p5.m5\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{E}_{i}=\\frac{1}{m}\\sum_{j=1}^{m}\\mathbf{e}_{j}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐄</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>m</mi></mfrac><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mrow><msubsup><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>m</mi></msubsup><msub><mi>𝐞</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{E}_{i}=\\frac{1}{m}\\sum_{j=1}^{m}\\mathbf{e}_{j}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S5.SS2\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">5.2. </span>Time-Series Modality Encoder \n<br class=\"ltx_break\">( <math id=\"S5.SS2.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\textbf{CAMEF}_{\\text{Time-Series}}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msub><mtext class=\"ltx_mathvariant_bold\">CAMEF</mtext><mtext>Time-Series</mtext></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\textbf{CAMEF}_{\\text{Time-Series}}</annotation></semantics></math> )</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S5.SS2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">To encode the time series data, we employ a pretrained time series encoder, MOMENT <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep\">(<a href=\"#bib.bib22\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Goswami et al., 2024</a>)</cite>, which generates a fixed-dimensional vector for an input time series segment. Subsequently, we design a multi-residual layer to further refine the encoding vectors, as shown below:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS2.p2\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<table id=\"S5.E4\" class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table\">\n\n<tbody><tr class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline\">\n<td rowspan=\"1\" class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left\">(4)</span></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft\"></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center\"><math id=\"S5.E4.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{\\mathcal{X}}_{i}=\\textbf{MOMENT}(\\{X_{1},X_{2},\\dots,X_{n}\\}),\" display=\"block\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒳</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext class=\"ltx_mathvariant_bold\">MOMENT</mtext><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">}</mo></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{\\mathcal{X}}_{i}=\\textbf{MOMENT}(\\{X_{1},X_{2},\\dots,X_{n}\\}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright\"></td></tr></tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS2.p3\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS2.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">where <math id=\"S5.SS2.p3.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{\\mathcal{X}}_{i}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{d}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒳</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{\\mathcal{X}}_{i}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math> is the encoded vector for the input time series segment <math id=\"S5.SS2.p3.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\{X_{1},X_{2},\\dots,X_{n}\\}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">{</mo><mrow><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>X</mi><mi>n</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\{X_{1},X_{2},\\dots,X_{n}\\}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id=\"S5.SS2.p3.m3\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"d\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">d</annotation></semantics></math> represents the dimensionality of the encoded vector. To enhance this representation, we introduce a multi-residual projection layer:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS2.p4\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<table id=\"S5.E5\" class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table\">\n\n<tbody><tr class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline\">\n<td rowspan=\"1\" class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left\">(5)</span></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft\"></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center\"><math id=\"S5.E5.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{Z}_{i}=\\mathbf{\\mathcal{X}}_{i}+f_{\\text{residual}}(\\mathbf{\\mathcal{X}}_{i}),\" display=\"block\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒳</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext>residual</mtext></msub><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒳</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{Z}_{i}=\\mathbf{\\mathcal{X}}_{i}+f_{\\text{residual}}(\\mathbf{\\mathcal{X}}_{i}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright\"></td></tr></tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS2.p5\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS2.p5.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">where <math id=\"S5.SS2.p5.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"f_{\\text{residual}}(\\mathbf{\\mathcal{X}}_{i})\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext>residual</mtext></msub><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒳</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">f_{\\text{residual}}(\\mathbf{\\mathcal{X}}_{i})</annotation></semantics></math> represents the transformation applied through the residual projection layer, which consists of multiple linear layers interleaved with GELU activations:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS2.p6\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<table id=\"S5.E6\" class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table\">\n\n<tbody><tr class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline\">\n<td rowspan=\"1\" class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left\">(6)</span></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft\"></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center\"><math id=\"S5.E6.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"f_{\\text{residual}}(\\mathbf{\\mathcal{X}}_{i})=\\mathbf{W}_{3}\\cdot\\text{GELU}(\\mathbf{W}_{2}\\cdot\\text{GELU}(\\mathbf{W}_{1}\\cdot\\mathbf{\\mathcal{X}}_{i}+\\mathbf{b}_{1})+\\mathbf{b}_{2})+\\mathbf{b}_{3},\" display=\"block\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mtext>residual</mtext></msub><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒳</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo lspace=\"0.222em\" rspace=\"0.222em\">⋅</mo><mtext>GELU</mtext></mrow><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo lspace=\"0.222em\" rspace=\"0.222em\">⋅</mo><mtext>GELU</mtext></mrow><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace=\"0.222em\" rspace=\"0.222em\">⋅</mo><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">𝒳</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝐛</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝐛</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>𝐛</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">f_{\\text{residual}}(\\mathbf{\\mathcal{X}}_{i})=\\mathbf{W}_{3}\\cdot\\text{GELU}(\\mathbf{W}_{2}\\cdot\\text{GELU}(\\mathbf{W}_{1}\\cdot\\mathbf{\\mathcal{X}}_{i}+\\mathbf{b}_{1})+\\mathbf{b}_{2})+\\mathbf{b}_{3},</annotation></semantics></math></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright\"></td></tr></tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS2.p7\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS2.p7.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">where <math id=\"S5.SS2.p7.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{W}_{1},\\mathbf{W}_{2}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{1024\\times 1024},\\mathbf{W}_{3}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{1024\\times 768}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mn>1024</mn><mo lspace=\"0.222em\" rspace=\"0.222em\">×</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mn>1024</mn><mo lspace=\"0.222em\" rspace=\"0.222em\">×</mo><mn>768</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{W}_{1},\\mathbf{W}_{2}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{1024\\times 1024},\\mathbf{W}_{3}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{1024\\times 768}</annotation></semantics></math> are the weight matrices, and <math id=\"S5.SS2.p7.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{b}_{1},\\mathbf{b}_{2}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{1024},\\mathbf{b}_{3}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{768}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐛</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐛</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>1024</mn></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><msub><mi>𝐛</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>768</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{b}_{1},\\mathbf{b}_{2}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{1024},\\mathbf{b}_{3}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{768}</annotation></semantics></math> are the respective biases. Finally, <math id=\"S5.SS2.p7.m3\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{Z}_{i}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{1024}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>𝐙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>1024</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{Z}_{i}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{1024}</annotation></semantics></math> serves as the refined vector for the time series segment.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S5.SS3\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">5.3. </span>Feature Fusion and Time Series Decoder</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S5.SS3.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS3.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">After obtaining the encoded vectors from the textual and time series data, denoted as <math id=\"S5.SS3.p1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{E}_{i}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐄</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{E}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id=\"S5.SS3.p1.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{Z}_{i}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{Z}_{i}</annotation></semantics></math>, respectively, we concatenate them to form a unified representation:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS3.p2\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<table id=\"S5.E7\" class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table\">\n\n<tbody><tr class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline\">\n<td rowspan=\"1\" class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left\">(7)</span></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft\"></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center\"><math id=\"S5.E7.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{E}_{\\text{combined}}=\\text{Concat}(\\mathbf{E}_{i},\\mathbf{Z}_{i}),\" display=\"block\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐄</mi><mtext>combined</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>Concat</mtext><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><msub><mi>𝐄</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>𝐙</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{E}_{\\text{combined}}=\\text{Concat}(\\mathbf{E}_{i},\\mathbf{Z}_{i}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright\"></td></tr></tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS3.p3\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS3.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">which captures both semantic content from macroeconomic texts and temporal patterns from time series inputs. To fuse these modalities, <math id=\"S5.SS3.p3.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{E}_{\\text{combined}}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐄</mi><mtext>combined</mtext></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{E}_{\\text{combined}}</annotation></semantics></math> is passed through a two-layer feedforward network with GELU activation:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS3.p4\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<table id=\"S5.E8\" class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table\">\n\n<tbody><tr class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline\">\n<td rowspan=\"1\" class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left\">(8)</span></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft\"></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center\"><math id=\"S5.E8.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{E}_{\\text{fused}}=\\mathbf{W}^{(f2)}\\cdot\\text{GELU}(\\mathbf{W}^{(f1)}\\cdot\\mathbf{E}*{\\text{combined}}+\\mathbf{b}^{(f1)})+\\mathbf{b}^{(f2)},\" display=\"block\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐄</mi><mtext>fused</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace=\"0.222em\" rspace=\"0.222em\">⋅</mo><mtext>GELU</mtext></mrow><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace=\"0.222em\" rspace=\"0.222em\">⋅</mo><mi>𝐄</mi></mrow><mo lspace=\"0.222em\" rspace=\"0.222em\">∗</mo><mtext>combined</mtext></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>𝐛</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>𝐛</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{E}_{\\text{fused}}=\\mathbf{W}^{(f2)}\\cdot\\text{GELU}(\\mathbf{W}^{(f1)}\\cdot\\mathbf{E}*{\\text{combined}}+\\mathbf{b}^{(f1)})+\\mathbf{b}^{(f2)},</annotation></semantics></math></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright\"></td></tr></tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS3.p5\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS3.p5.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">where <math id=\"S5.SS3.p5.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{W}^{(f1)}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{(2\\times 768)\\times 1024}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace=\"0.222em\" rspace=\"0.222em\">×</mo><mn>768</mn></mrow><mo rspace=\"0.055em\" stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace=\"0.222em\">×</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{W}^{(f1)}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{(2\\times 768)\\times 1024}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id=\"S5.SS3.p5.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{W}^{(f2)}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{1024\\times 1024}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mn>1024</mn><mo lspace=\"0.222em\" rspace=\"0.222em\">×</mo><mn>1024</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{W}^{(f2)}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{1024\\times 1024}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id=\"S5.SS3.p5.m3\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{b}^{(f1)},\\mathbf{b}^{(f2)}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{1024}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐛</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo><mrow><msup><mi>𝐛</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><mi>f</mi><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mn>1024</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{b}^{(f1)},\\mathbf{b}^{(f2)}\\in\\mathbb{R}^{1024}</annotation></semantics></math> are the corresponding weight matrices and bias terms. This fusion block enables interaction across modalities and produces a refined joint embedding for downstream decoding.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS3.p6\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS3.p6.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">We then employ GPT-2 <cite class=\"ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep\">(<a href=\"#bib.bib42\" title=\"\" class=\"ltx_ref\">Radford et al., 2019</a>)</cite> as the decoder to decode the fused vector by leveraging its effective auto-regressive ability:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS3.p7\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<table id=\"S5.E9\" class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table\">\n\n<tbody><tr class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline\">\n<td rowspan=\"1\" class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{H}^{(0)}=\\mathbf{E}_{\\text{fused}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id=\"S5.SS3.p8.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"f_{\\text{GPT2\\_layer}}^{(l)}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msubsup><mi>f</mi><mtext>GPT2_layer</mtext><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mi>l</mi><mo id=\"S5.SS3.p8.m3\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"l\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>l</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">l</annotation></semantics></math>-th GPT-2 layer, where <math id=\"S5.SS3.p8.m4\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"l=12\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mi>l</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">l=12</annotation></semantics></math>. After the final layer, the output is normalized using a layer normalization function:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS3.p9\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<table id=\"S5.E10\" class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table\">\n\n<tbody><tr class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline\">\n<td rowspan=\"1\" class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_eqn_center_padright\"></td></tr></tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS3.p10\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS3.p10.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The final output <math id=\"S5.SS3.p10.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{H}_{\\text{final}}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>final</mtext></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{H}_{\\text{final}}</annotation></semantics></math> is then used to generate predictions based on the combined multi-modal information.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S5.SS4\" class=\"ltx_subsection\">\n<h3 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">5.4. </span>Time-Series Forecasting Post-Regressor and Learning Objectives</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S5.SS4.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS4.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">We designed a <span id=\"S5.SS4.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Post-Regressor</span> that applies a linear transformation to the concatenated vector <math id=\"S5.SS4.p1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{H}_{\\text{final}}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>final</mtext></msub><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{H}_{\\text{final}}</annotation></semantics></math>, followed by GELU activation and a dropout layer with a rate of 0.1:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS4.p2\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<table id=\"S5.E11\" class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table\">\n\n<tbody><tr class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline\">\n<td rowspan=\"1\" class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left\">(11)</span></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft\"></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center\"><math id=\"S5.E11.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{R}^{(k)}=\\text{GELU}(\\mathbf{W}^{(k)}\\cdot\\mathbf{R}^{(k-1)}+\\mathbf{b}^{(k)}),\" display=\"block\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐑</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mtext>GELU</mtext><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><mrow><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo lspace=\"0.222em\" rspace=\"0.222em\">⋅</mo><msup><mi>𝐑</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>+</mo><msup><mi>𝐛</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{R}^{(k)}=\\text{GELU}(\\mathbf{W}^{(k)}\\cdot\\mathbf{R}^{(k-1)}+\\mathbf{b}^{(k)}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright\"></td></tr></tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS4.p3\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS4.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">where <math id=\"S5.SS4.p3.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{R}^{(0)}=\\mathbf{H}_{\\text{final}}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝐑</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>𝐇</mi><mtext>final</mtext></msub></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{R}^{(0)}=\\mathbf{H}_{\\text{final}}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id=\"S5.SS4.p3.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{W}^{(k)}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐖</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{W}^{(k)}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id=\"S5.SS4.p3.m3\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{b}^{(k)}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msup><mi>𝐛</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow></msup><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{b}^{(k)}</annotation></semantics></math> are the weight matrix and bias of the <math id=\"S5.SS4.p3.m4\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"k\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">k</annotation></semantics></math>-th linear layer, respectively. <math id=\"S5.SS4.p3.m5\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"k=4\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">k=4</annotation></semantics></math> is the total number of layers in the regressor. The final linear layer maps the representation to a vector of shape <math id=\"S5.SS4.p3.m6\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"(d\\times\\text{pred\\_len})\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace=\"0.222em\" rspace=\"0.222em\">×</mo><mtext>pred_len</mtext></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">(d\\times\\text{pred\\_len})</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id=\"S5.SS4.p3.m7\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"d\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">d</annotation></semantics></math> is the forecast dimensionality and <span id=\"S5.SS4.p3.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_markedasmath\">pred_len</span> is the number of predicted time steps:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS4.p4\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<table id=\"S5.E12\" class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table\">\n\n<tbody><tr class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline\">\n<td rowspan=\"1\" class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left\">(12)</span></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft\"></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center\"><math id=\"S5.E12.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{\\hat{Y}}=\\mathbf{W}_{\\text{out}}\\cdot\\mathbf{R}^{(K)}+\\mathbf{b}_{\\text{out}},\" display=\"block\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mover accent=\"true\"><mi>𝐘</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐖</mi><mtext>out</mtext></msub><mo lspace=\"0.222em\" rspace=\"0.222em\">⋅</mo><msup><mi>𝐑</mi><mrow><mo encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{\\hat{Y}}=\\mathbf{W}_{\\text{out}}\\cdot\\mathbf{R}^{(K)}+\\mathbf{b}_{\\text{out}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright\"></td></tr></tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS4.p5\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS4.p5.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">where <math id=\"S5.SS4.p5.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{\\hat{Y}}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mover accent=\"true\"><mi>𝐘</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{\\hat{Y}}</annotation></semantics></math>, represents the predicted time series values.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS4.p6\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS4.p6.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S5.SS4.p6.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Learning Objectives for Time Series:</span> We employ a combination of Mean Squared Error (MSE) loss and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) loss to optimize the model. The MSE loss minimizes the squared differences between the predicted time series values, <math id=\"S5.SS4.p6.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{\\hat{Y}}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mover accent=\"true\"><mi>𝐘</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{\\hat{Y}}</annotation></semantics></math>, and the ground truth values, <math id=\"S5.SS4.p6.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbf{Y}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>𝐘</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbf{Y}</annotation></semantics></math>, while the MAE loss minimizes the absolute differences. These are defined as:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS4.p7\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<table id=\"S5.E13\" class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table\">\n\n<tbody><tr class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline\">\n<td rowspan=\"1\" class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left\">(13)</span></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft\"></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center\"><math id=\"S5.E13.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{L}_{\\text{MSE}}=\\frac{1}{n}\\sum_{i=1}^{n}(\\mathbf{\\hat{Y}}_{i}-\\mathbf{Y}_{i})^{2},\\quad\\mathcal{L}_{\\text{MAE}}=\\frac{1}{n}\\sum_{i=1}^{n}|\\mathbf{\\hat{Y}}_{i}-\\mathbf{Y}_{i}|,\" display=\"block\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℒ</mi><mtext>MSE</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits=\"false\" rspace=\"0em\">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><msup><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">(</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent=\"true\"><mi>𝐘</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐘</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">)</mo></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace=\"1.167em\">,</mo><mrow><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℒ</mi><mtext>MAE</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mi>n</mi></mfrac><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mrow><munderover><mo movablelimits=\"false\" rspace=\"0em\">∑</mo><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>n</mi></munderover><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">|</mo><mrow><msub><mover accent=\"true\"><mi>𝐘</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>𝐘</mi><mi>i</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">|</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{L}_{\\text{MSE}}=\\frac{1}{n}\\sum_{i=1}^{n}(\\mathbf{\\hat{Y}}_{i}-\\mathbf{Y}_{i})^{2},\\quad\\mathcal{L}_{\\text{MAE}}=\\frac{1}{n}\\sum_{i=1}^{n}|\\mathbf{\\hat{Y}}_{i}-\\mathbf{Y}_{i}|,</annotation></semantics></math></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright\"></td></tr></tbody>\n</table>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS4.p8\" class=\"ltx_para ltx_noindent\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS4.p8.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">where <math id=\"S5.SS4.p8.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"n\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">n</annotation></semantics></math> is the number of predicted values (e.g., 35, 70, or 140, as defined in Section <a href=\"#S6.SS1\" title=\"6.1. Experimental Settings ‣ 6. Experiments ‣ CAMEF: Causal-Augmented Multi-Modality Event-Driven Financial Forecasting by Integrating Time Series Patterns and Salient Macroeconomic Announcements\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">6.1</span></a>). The total loss function combines both objectives to balance optimization for large and small errors:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS4.p9\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<table id=\"S5.E14\" class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table\">\n\n<tbody><tr class=\"ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline\">\n<td rowspan=\"1\" class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left\">(14)</span></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft\"></td>\n<td class=\"ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center\"><math id=\"S5.E14.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{L}_{\\text{Time}}=\\mathcal{L}_{\\text{MSE}}+\\mathcal{L}_{\\text{MAE}}.\" display=\"block\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℒ</mi><mtext>Time</mtext></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℒ</mi><mtext>MSE</mtext></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection\">5.5. </span>Counterfactual Events Sampling and Causal Learning Objective</h3>\n\n<div id=\"S5.SS5.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS5.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">Causal learning enhances the robustness of the CAMEF model by enabling it to identify the correct event script among sampled counterfactual events (CEs). To achieve this, we first design a <span id=\"S5.SS5.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Diverse Counterfactual Event Sampling Mechanism</span>, which generates two types of CEs. These counterfactuals, along with their corresponding time-series data, are then encoded using the textual and time-series modalities of CAMEF. This process helps the model learn causal relationships between events and their corresponding time-series movements.</p>\n</div>\n<section id=\"S5.SS5.SSS1\" class=\"ltx_subsubsection\">\n<h4 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection\">5.5.1. </span>Diverse Counterfactual Event Sampling Mechanism</h4>\n\n<div id=\"S5.SS5.SSS1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS5.SSS1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">We propose a <span id=\"S5.SS5.SSS1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Diverse Counterfactual Event Sampling Mechanism</span> to enhance the model’s ability to both identify the ground-truth event and distinguish between different event types. This mechanism is designed with two objectives: (1) to help the model recognize the ground-truth event among similar counterfactuals of the same type, and (2) to enable the model to differentiate between events of different types.</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS5.SSS1.p2\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS5.SSS1.p2.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">To achieve these objectives, we generate two categories of counterfactual events for each factual event:</p>\n<ol id=\"S5.I1\" class=\"ltx_enumerate\">\n<li id=\"S5.I1.i1\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">(1)</span> \n<div id=\"S5.I1.i1.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S5.I1.i1.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S5.I1.i1.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Identical Type Sampling:</span> Counterfactual events of the same type as the ground-truth event, created by modifying sentiment-relevant components and key numerical variables, as detailed in Sec. <a href=\"#S4.SS2\" title=\"4.2. Counterfactual Events Generation based on LLM ‣ 4. Data Collection and Counterfactual Event Augmentation ‣ CAMEF: Causal-Augmented Multi-Modality Event-Driven Financial Forecasting by Integrating Time Series Patterns and Salient Macroeconomic Announcements\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">4.2</span></a>.</p>\n</div></li>\n<li id=\"S5.I1.i2\" class=\"ltx_item\" style=\"list-style-type:none;\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_item\">(2)</span> \n<div id=\"S5.I1.i2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S5.I1.i2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\"><span id=\"S5.I1.i2.p1.1.1\" class=\"ltx_text ltx_font_bold\">Diverse Type Sampling:</span> Counterfactual events of a different type, sampled by substituting the ground-truth event with 5 other event type occurring on the closest date.</p>\n</div></li>\n</ol>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS5.SSS1.p3\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS5.SSS1.p3.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">This mechanism provides a diverse set of counterfactual events, collectively denoted as <math id=\"S5.SS5.SSS1.p3.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathbb{E}^{CF}:=\\{\\mathcal{E}^{CF}_{1},\\mathcal{E}^{CF}_{2},\\ldots,\\mathcal{E}^{CF}_{|\\mathbb{E}^{CF}|}\\}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mi>F</mi></mrow></msup><mo>:=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">{</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mn>1</mn><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mi>F</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mn>2</mn><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mi>F</mi></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant=\"normal\">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">|</mo><msup><mi>𝔼</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mi>F</mi></mrow></msup><mo stretchy=\"false\">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mi>F</mi></mrow></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy=\"false\">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathbb{E}^{CF}:=\\{\\mathcal{E}^{CF}_{1},\\mathcal{E}^{CF}_{2},\\ldots,\\mathcal{E}^{CF}_{|\\mathbb{E}^{CF}|}\\}</annotation></semantics></math>, we set the total number of diverse-type samples to be 5, and the default number of identical-type samples to be 10 as introduced Sec. <a href=\"#S4.SS2\" title=\"4.2. Counterfactual Events Generation based on LLM ‣ 4. Data Collection and Counterfactual Event Augmentation ‣ CAMEF: Causal-Augmented Multi-Modality Event-Driven Financial Forecasting by Integrating Time Series Patterns and Salient Macroeconomic Announcements\" class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">4.2</span></a>.</p>\n</div>\n</section>\n<section id=\"S5.SS5.SSS2\" class=\"ltx_subsubsection\">\n<h4 class=\"ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection\"><span class=\"ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection\">5.5.2. </span>Causal Learning Objective</h4>\n\n<div id=\"S5.SS5.SSS2.p1\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<p id=\"S5.SS5.SSS2.p1.1\" class=\"ltx_p\">The causal learning process utilizes both the textual (see Sec. <a href=\"#S5.SS1\" title='5.1. Textual Modality Encoder (\"CAMEF\"_\"Textual\") ‣ 5. CAMEF Architecture ‣ CAMEF: Causal-Augmented Multi-Modality Event-Driven Financial Forecasting by Integrating Time Series Patterns and Salient Macroeconomic Announcements' class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">5.1</span></a>) and time-series (see Sec. <a href=\"#S5.SS2\" title='5.2. Time-Series Modality Encoder ( \"CAMEF\"_\"Time-Series\" ) ‣ 5. CAMEF Architecture ‣ CAMEF: Causal-Augmented Multi-Modality Event-Driven Financial Forecasting by Integrating Time Series Patterns and Salient Macroeconomic Announcements' class=\"ltx_ref\"><span class=\"ltx_text ltx_ref_tag\">5.2</span></a>) encoders of CAMEF to capture the relationships between events and market movements. The textual encoder is used to encode both the ground-truth event <math id=\"S5.SS5.SSS2.p1.m1\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}^{GT}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}^{GT}</annotation></semantics></math> and the sampled CEs <math id=\"S5.SS5.SSS2.p1.m2\" class=\"ltx_Math\" alttext=\"\\mathcal{E}^{CF}\" display=\"inline\" intent=\":literal\"><semantics><msup><mi class=\"ltx_font_mathcaligraphic\">ℰ</mi><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo lspace=\"0em\" rspace=\"0em\">​</mo><mi>F</mi></mrow></msup><annotation encoding=\"application/x-tex\">\\mathcal{E}^{CF}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>\n</div>\n<div id=\"S5.SS5.SSS2.p2\" class=\"ltx_para\">\n<table id=\"S5.E15\" class=\"ltx_equation
