      "front_matter": "                                                F EW-S HOT L EARNING PATTERNS IN F INANCIAL T IME -S ERIES\n                                                           FOR T REND -F OLLOWING S TRATEGIES\n\n\n\n                                                                       Kieran Wood∗                                       Samuel Kessler∗\n                                                                     Oxford-Man Institute                               Oxford-Man Institute\n\n\n\n\narXiv:2310.10500v2 [q-fin.TR] 28 Mar 2024\n                                                                     University of Oxford                               University of Oxford\n                                                                 kieran.wood@eng.ox.ac.uk                          samuel.kessler@eng.ox.ac.uk\n\n                                                                      Stephen J. Roberts                                    Stefan Zohren\n                                                                      Oxford-Man Institute                                Oxford-Man Institute\n                                                                      University of Oxford                                University of Oxford\n                                                                stephen.roberts@eng.ox.ac.uk                         stefan.zohren@eng.ox.ac.uk\n\n\n                                                                                                   March 29, 2024\n\n                                                                                                    A BSTRACT\n                                                         Forecasting models for systematic trading strategies do not adapt quickly when financial market\n                                                         conditions rapidly change, as was seen in the advent of the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020, causing\n                                                         many forecasting models to take loss-making positions. To deal with such situations, we propose a\n                                                         novel time-series trend-following forecaster that can quickly adapt to new market conditions, referred\n                                                         to as regimes.",
      "selected_passages": [
        {
          "term": "Conclusions and Future Work",
          "match_count_pages": 1,
          "passages": [
            {
              "physical_page": 15,
              "text": "re, we direct readers to [54]. For a more general overview\nof deep-learning techniques for time-series forecasting we direct readers to [55].\n\n\n\n\n7   Conclusions and Future Work\n\n\nWe introduce X-Trend: the Cross Attentive Time-Series Trend Network. It leverages few-shot learning and change-\npoint detection to enable adaptation to new financial regimes. We show that it is able to recover from the COVID-19\ndraw-down almost twice as quickly as an equivalent neural time-series agent. Over the 5-year period 2018 to 2023,\nwe are able to improve risk-adjusted returns by 18.9% compared to the baseline agent and around 10-fold compared\nto a conventional Time-series Momentum (TSMOM) strategy. This boost in performance is largely driven by our\ncross-attention step which transfers trends, from similar patterns in a context set. Furthermore, our model can generate\nprofitable zero-shot trading signals in an extremely challenging low-resource setting where we trade a previously unseen\nasset we achieve a Sharpe of 0.47 compared to loss-making time-series momentum baselines, both deep-learning based\nand conventional TSMOM. In this work we withheld assets from a standard dataset to test zero-shot performance; a\nfuture avenue of work could be applying this framework to an emerging asset class such as cryptocurrencies.\nWe illustrate the importance of constructing a good context set, where we improve Sharpe by 11.3% after segmenting the\nsequences with change-point detection. A future avenue of work would be to further investigate context set con"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "context set",
          "match_count_pages": 13,
          "passages": [
            {
              "physical_page": 1,
              "text": "Cross Attentive Time-Series Trend Network – X-Trend – which takes\n                                                         positions attending over a context set of financial time-series regimes. X-Trend transfers trends\n                                                         from similar patterns in the context set to make forecasts, then subsequently takes positions for a\n                                                         new distinct target regime. By quickly adapting to new financial regimes, X-Trend increases Sharpe\n                                                         ratio by 18.9% over a neural forecaster and 10-fold over a conventional Time-series Momentum\n                                                         strategy during the turbulent market period from 2018 to 2023. Our strategy recovers twice as quickly\n                                                         from the COVID-19 drawdown compared to the neural-forecaster. X-Trend can also take zero-shot\n                                                         positions on novel unseen financial assets obtaining a 5-fold Sharpe ratio increase versus a neural\n                                                         time-series trend forecaster over the same period. Furthermore, the cross-attention mechanism allows\n                                                         us to interpret the relationship between forecasts and patterns in the context set.\n\n                                            Keywords Trend-Following · Time-Series Momentum · Few-S"
            },
            {
              "physical_page": 2,
              "text": "view of the X-Trend few-shot learning trend-following model. 1) Each asset is segmented into\nregimes using a change-point detection algorithm. 2) The context set is constructed by randomly sampling regimes from\ndifferent assets. The objective is to produce long/short positions given the target sequence while respecting causality\nwith the context set. 3) Our X-Trend model uses a cross-attention layer for the target to leverage patterns in the context\nset. 4) The model produces a distribution over next-day returns. 5) The model outputs positions using Predictive\nprobability density function To traded Position module (PTP). 6) We train our model by jointly optimizing a Sharpe\nratio loss and negative log-likelihood.\n\n\nIn recent years it has been observed, that the risk-adjusted returns of conventional Time-series Momentum (TSMOM)\nmodels [5], which exploit trends in financial time-series, have deteriorated by 87.4% from 2018 to 2023 compared to\nthe period from 1995 to 2000. This can potentially be attributed to a concept known as ‘factor crowding’ [6], where\narbitrageurs trade the same assets based on similar factors. This causes market inefficiencies to quickly disappear and\ncan increase the risk of liquidity-driven tail events [7]. To mitigate this, one alternative has been to explore new assets\nwhere we typically do not have sufficient data for deep learning approaches.\nIn deep learning, quick adaptation to new data or few-shot learning has seen recent advances in computer vision\n[8, 9, 10]. Few-shot learning involves training"
            }
          ]
        },
        {
          "term": "daily",
          "match_count_pages": 3,
          "passages": [
            {
              "physical_page": 3,
              "text": " optimal trading signal and\n             forecast.\n\n\n2         Preliminaries\n                                 (i)\nLet us denote a time-series p1:t of daily close prices, where i denotes a particular asset from a basket of assets i ∈ I\n                                                                                                                      (i)\nand t denotes a time index t ∈ {1, . . . , T } where T is the final observation for the asset. We work with returns r1:t ,\nwhich linearly de-trends the price series:\n                                                                  (i)         (i)\n                                                     (i)         pt − pt−t′\n                                                    rt−t′ ,t =          (i)\n                                                                                    ,                                        (1)\n                                                                      pt−t′\n                                                                                        (i)            (i)\nwhere t′ is the number of days we calculate returns over and for brevity we use rt to denote rt−1,t .\n                                        (i)\nOur objective is to trade a position zt ∈ [−1, 1] which we hold for the next day t + 1 conditioned on a target sequence\n  (i)                                (i)\nx−lt :t of the lt last days, where xt ∈ X is a vector of |X | factors measuring trends at different timescales or the\nrelationship between trends at different timescales. The"
            },
            {
              "physical_page": 13,
              "text": " 60-day ex-ante volatility is doing a good job because we\ncan observe that the 95% confidence interval is fairly stable around ±1.96 when targeting a daily volatility of 1.\nFor X-Trend-Q (Fig. 8), we observe that the trading signal deviates more from the predictive median than X-Trend-G,\nindicating that it incorporates the full predictive distribution into the trading signal. This is likely the reason that the\nSharpe for X-Trend-Q outperforms X-Trend-G by 7.1% in the few-shot setting over the turbulent period of 2018 to\n2023. This supports our hypothesis that, for the best results, Gaussianity of returns should not be assumed in the\nfew-shot setting. The assumption of Gaussian returns may be more appropriate in the low-resource setting.\nWe provide an illustrative example of how we can interpret the cross-attention weights in Fig. 9 for the natural gas\nfutures contract in 2022; a period exhibiting significant trends due to the Russia-Ukraine conflict. We examine 3 points\nin time, which correspond to 3 different regimes, and in all cases, the top 3 attention weights are highly intuitive.               "physical_page": 2,
              "text": " that\ncan make predictions in new market regimes and unseen markets. In practice, our experiments backtest on continuous\nfutures contracts of various asset classes: equities, foreign exchange, commodities and fixed income. Our model obtains\nsignificantly higher risk-adjusted returns in terms of Sharpe ratio [16], a measure of returns per unit volatility. Our\nmodel is able to learn transferable patterns, then subsequently learn to take positions in markets or regimes distinct\nfrom those used for training. The idea of universal patterns in financial markets, which are transferable, is motivated by\nthe works [17, 18, 19].\nOur model uses a cross-attention mechanism over a context-set [20, 21]. Attention mechanisms [22] have been shown\nto improve returns by attending over an asset’s history [19], this work generalizes this finding by extending the temporal\nattention mechanism over other assets. This enables our model to transfer knowledge from the context set to enable\nbetter predictions for a new regime or new market with little data. Different regimes from financial assets are segmented\nusing change-point detection methods [23, 24]. Additionally, the attention maps provide a degree of interpretability in\nthe resulting predictions [25, 19]. We also use the latest insights from deep time-series momentum strategies to train our\nmodel to produce positive returns over our baselines [3]. We call our method the Cross Attentive Time-Series Trend\nNetwork or X-Trend for short. The code is available at https://github.com/kieranjwood/x-tre"

See Appendix B for further details.\nWe backtest our X-Trend variants on a portfolio of 50 of the most liquid, continuous futures contracts6 , I, over the period\nfrom 1990 to 2023, extracted from the Pinnacle Data Corp CLC Database7 . The futures contracts we have selected are\namongst the most liquid and typical for backtesting TSMOM strategies [5, 30, 3, 19]. To test-out-of-sample across the\nentire history, we use an expanding window approach, where we initially train on 1990 to 1995, test out-of-sample\non the period from 1995 to 2000, expand the training window to from 1990 to 2000, then test out-of-sample on the\nsubsequent 5 years and so on. We take particular note of performance over the 2020 to 2022 period, which covers the\nCOVID-19 crisis, exhibiting dynamics that are significantly different to the training set.\n For our zero-shot experiments, we randomly selected 20 of the 50 Pinnacle dataset assets as the test set, Its , leaving\n the other 30, Itr for the context set and training.               "text": "arning [40]. Learning distances between a few context points and a new target point has been fruitful for\nfew-shot image classification [10, 41, 42]. Neural processes learn to sample functions like Gaussian Process [43, 37, 20].\nAutomatic context construction for few-shot learning using change-point detection methods has also been explored for\nimage datasets [44]. Recently there have been works that challenge some of the common assumptions for few-shot\nimage classification [45, 46, 47].\nFew-shot learning for time-series. Neural Processes [37] which parameterize a distribution over functions have been\nemployed for few-shot learning for time-series forecasting [48]. Neural processes algorithmically use a latent variable\nto enable drawing a new function for each point by sampling; the latent variable can employ autoregressive transition\ndynamics for time-series [49]. One can condition the target time-series predictions on a context of time-series with\na cross-attention mechanism [38]. The cross-attention mechanism has been shown to be very effective for Neural\nProcesses [20]. Gradient-based few-shot learning has also been successfully employed for time-series [50]. From the\nliterature and from our own initial experiments on toy data (Appendix B) we found the cross-attention very effective for\nfew-shot learning for time-series.\nDeep-learning for financial time-series. # 100 Aspects of Introducing Few-Shot Learning into Intraday Algorithmic Trading

## Executive Methodological Evaluation
This audit evaluates the theoretical validity, empirical feasibility, and academic publication quality of introducing **Few-Shot Learning (FSL) and Meta-Learning** into an intraday 15m trading signal engine (combining Chandelier Exit heuristics, Binance order flow, and scheduled macroeconomic events).

Each aspect is scored on a **0 to 100 Q1 Quality Gap Scale**:
- **90–100:** Top-Tier Q1 Research Gap (Publishable in *Journal of Financial Economics*, *Journal of Machine Learning Research*, *ACM ICAIF*, *NeurIPS*).
- **80–89:** Solid Q1/Q2 Academic Contribution (*Quantitative Finance*, *Journal of Financial Data Science*, *IEEE Access*).
- **70–79:** Applied / Practitioner Gap (Valuable for proprietary trading firms, but incremental academic novelty).
- **< 70:** Dangerous / Overfitting Gimmick (High statistical bias, data snooping trap, or unpublishable).

---

## 1. Regime Shift & Fast Adaptation

### Aspect 1: Post-FOMC Volatility Expansion Adaptation
- **Description:** Adapting a 15m breakout model within K=5 bars following an unexpected rate hike.
- **Q1 Gap Score:** **92/100**
- **Methodological Audit:** Q1 Gap: Standard models suffer severe transient drawdown during sudden central bank policy shifts; few-shot fast adaptation is novel in high-frequency regimes.

### Aspect 2: Flash Crash / Liquidation Cascade Rapid Re-anchoring
- **Description:** Few-shot re-estimation of support barriers after a >10% cascade.
- **Q1 Gap Score:** **88/100**
- **Methodological Audit:** Q1 Gap: Liquidation cascades break Gaussian/GARCH assumptions; fast meta-updating solves structural covariance breakdown.

### Aspect 3: Low-Volatility Squeeze Transition
- **Description:** Recognizing transition from mean-reversion compression to trend expansion via K-shot samples.
- **Q1 Gap Score:** **85/100**
- **Methodological Audit:** Q1 Gap: Pre-breakout regimes have very few historical examples per year, making standard deep learning sample-starved.

### Aspect 4: Weekend-to-Monday Session Open Gap Adaptation
- **Description:** Calibrating risk parameters from Sunday open to Monday NY cash open in K bars.
- **Q1 Gap Score:** **74/100**
- **Methodological Audit:** Marginal Q1: Session transitions are well-studied via GARCH, but few-shot meta-learning offers an architectural alternative.

### Aspect 5: Multi-Horizon Volatility Regime Switching
- **Description:** Joint adaptation across 15m and 4h ATR scales using prototypical clusters.
- **Q1 Gap Score:** **89/100**
- **Methodological Audit:** Q1 Gap: Multi-scale temporal meta-learning addresses the curse of non-stationarity across disjoint frequencies.

### Aspect 6: Post-Halving Crypto Macro Regime Reset
- **Description:** Adapting historical four-year cycle features to post-halving structural supply dynamics.
- **Q1 Gap Score:** **68/100**
- **Methodological Audit:** B-tier Gap: Small sample size (only 4 halvings in history); prone to extreme statistical bias and small-N overfitting.

### Aspect 7: Emergency Bank Run / Sovereign Crisis Shock Calibration
- **Description:** Few-shot calibration during exogenous contagion events (e.g. SVB collapse).
- **Q1 Gap Score:** **91/100**
- **Methodological Audit:** Q1 Gap: Extreme tail-risk regime adaptation is a top open problem in quantitative risk management (JFE/JFQA quality).

### Aspect 8: Intraday Session Handover (London to NY Overlap)
- **Description:** Fast tuning of order flow delta thresholds during cross-continental session handovers.
- **Q1 Gap Score:** **78/100**
- **Methodological Audit:** Applied Gap: Strong practical value for prop firms; moderate academic novelty without deep theoretical framing.

### Aspect 9: Structural Shift in Market Maker Algorithmic Density
- **Description:** Adapting to sudden changes in market maker quote cancellation rates.
- **Q1 Gap Score:** **86/100**
- **Methodological Audit:** Q1 Gap: Directly bridges high-frequency microstructure (Hasbrouck) with meta-learning architectures.

### Aspect 10: Sudden Spread Blowout Recovery Regimes
- **Description:** Dynamic barrier recalculation when bid-ask spread widens by >5x normal standard deviation.
- **Q1 Gap Score:** **82/100**
- **Methodological Audit:** Solid Q1/Q2 Gap: Tackles execution-level friction in few-shot trading; highly relevant for empirical market microstructure.

## 2. Meta-Learning Architectures & Optimization

- **Description:** Applying second-order gradient MAML to optimize initial weights for rapid 15m directional fine-tuning.
- **Q1 Gap Score:** **90/100**

# Market-Moving News Taxonomy & Dataset Ingestion Architecture

## 1. News Classification Taxonomy

News events affecting financial markets—particularly Bitcoin (BTC) and broader liquid macro assets (Gold/NQ)—fall into five distinct categories based on predictability, transmission mechanism, and volatility duration.

---

### Category 1: Scheduled Tier-1 Macroeconomic Announcements
*Characteristics: High predictability of timing (exact second known in advance), severe 15m volatility spikes, spread blowouts, and order-book liquidity withdrawal.*

- **FOMC Interest Rate Decision & Policy Statement:** The benchmark rate decision by the US Federal Reserve. Dictates global dollar liquidity, borrowing costs, and risk-asset discount rates.
- **FOMC Press Conference (Fed Chair Q&A):** Fed Chair's live speech 30 minutes after rate decisions; causes violent whipsaws based on hawkish vs. dovish phrasing.
- **CPI (Consumer Price Index) & Core PCE:** Primary inflation gauges. Higher-than-expected inflation prompts higher interest rate expectations (bearish for BTC/equities, volatile for Gold).
- **NFP (Non-Farm Payrolls) & Unemployment Rate:** US labor market health. Strong jobs data signals economic resilience but increases Fed hawkishness.
- **GDP (Advance/Second Releases):** National economic growth gauge. Signals expansion vs. recessionary contraction.
- **PPI (Producer Price Index):** Wholesale inflation pipeline leading indicator.

---

### Category 2: Crypto-Specific Regulatory & Institutional Catalyst News
*Characteristics: Semi-scheduled or breaking news that directly alters the legal status, capital access, or regulatory perimeter of Bitcoin.*

- **SEC / CFTC Regulatory Actions & Lawsuits:** Enforcement actions against major exchanges (Binance, Coinbase) or classification rulings on digital assets.
- **Spot ETF Approvals & Net Daily Flows:** Daily net inflows/outflows from institutional spot ETFs (e.g., BlackRock IBIT, Fidelity FBTC). Institutional flow reports release every evening.
- **Sovereign Adoption & Strategic Reserve Legislation:** Bills regarding national Bitcoin reserves or legal tender adoption (e.g., El Salvador, US Strategic Bitcoin Reserve bills).
- **Corporate Treasury Disclosures:** Regular 8-K SEC filings from corporate buyers (e.g., MicroStrategy / Strategy purchases).

---

### Category 3: Systemic Counterparty & Microstructure Shock News
*Characteristics: Unscheduled "Black Swan" events causing severe one-sided liquidation cascades, basis dislocations, and market-maker withdrawals.*

- **Exchange Insolvency, Run, or Legal Seizure:** Historical precedents: Mt. Gox, FTX, Bitfinex. Direct threats to custodial funds and exchange matching engines.
- **Stablecoin Depegging & Reserve Scrutiny:** Runs on major stablecoins (USDT, USDC, UST). Because crypto is priced in USDT/USDC, a stablecoin depeg causes immediate artificial price distortions.
- **Government Seizure Liquidation Transfers:** On-chain movements of seized Bitcoin by sovereign entities (e.g., US Department of Justice Silk Road wallets, German BKA seized coins moving to exchanges).
- **Major Protocol / Bridge Hacks:** Multi-hundred-million-dollar exploits causing contagion.

---

### Category 4: Geopolitical & Macro Risk-Off Shocks
*Characteristics: Asymmetric exogenous shocks impacting global liquidity, commodity prices, and currency valuations.*

- **Military Conflicts & Escalations:** Missile strikes, invasions, or regional war escalations. Often triggers initial liquidity flight into cash/gold and liquidations in high-beta crypto.
- **Trade Sanctions & Tariff Announcements:** Executive orders imposing import tariffs or trade barriers, disrupting global supply chains and currency pegs.
- **Sovereign Debt Downgrades & Banking Panics:** Credit rating agency downgrades (Moody's, S&P) of sovereign debt or regional bank distress (e.g., SVB collapse).

---

### Category 5: Influential Market Commentary & Social Sentiment
*Characteristics: High-frequency narrative shifts driven by prominent market figures or viral retail trends.*

- **Central Bank Speeches (Inter-meeting):** Comments by voting Fed governors (Waller, Bowman, Williams).
- **High-Profile Market Commentators:** Statements from major hedge fund managers, tech executives, or political figures.
- **Viral Social Sentiment Spikes:** Coordinated retail momentum or panic sentiment surges across Twitter/X, Reddit (`r/Bitcoin`, `r/CryptoCurrency`), and Telegram.

---

## 2. Ingestion Strategy & Concrete Datasets (Free & Verified)

To train a Machine Learning model without lookahead bias, news datasets must contain **exact publication timestamps** down to the minute:

### 1. Local US Macroeconomic Calendar (Already Available Locally on Disk)
- **Path:** `/home/rarebat/ict-silver-bullet/data/training/calendar_us_2021_2026.csv`
- **Coverage:** 2021-01-08 to 2026-12-16 (192 clean point-in-time events).
- **Events:** Exact release timestamps for FOMC, CPI, and NFP.
- **Features Generated:**
  - `minutes_to_next_event`: Signed integer representing the distance in minutes to the next high-impact release.
  - `event_risk_zone`: Binary flag (1 if within ±30 minutes of event, 0 otherwise).
  - `event_type`: Categorical one-hot encoding (FOMC, CPI, NFP).

### 2. Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index (100% Free Public API)
- **Endpoint:** `https://api.alternative.me/fng/?limit=0`
- **Coverage:** Complete daily historical time series from 2018 to present.
- **Fields:**
  - `value`: Daily continuous sentiment score between 0 (Extreme Fear) and 100 (Extreme Greed).
  - `value_classification`: Categorical regime tag.
- **Features Generated:**
  - `fng_score`: Current regime sentiment value.
  - `fng_delta_7d`: 7-day momentum change in market sentiment.

### 3. Federal Reserve Official Public Announcements (Free RSS & XML Feeds)
- **Source:** `federalreserve.gov/feeds/press_monetary.xml`
- **Coverage:** All official monetary policy statements and transcripts.
- **Features Generated:**
  - `fed_statement_word_count`: Length and complexity of the statement.
  - `fed_tone_score`: FinBERT sentiment analysis applied to policy text.

### 4. Natural Language Sentiment Pipelines (Open Source)
- **HuggingFace Hub Datasets:** Pre-scraped historical financial and crypto headline archives (e.g., `financial_phrasebank`, `crypto-news-2020-2025`).
- **Transformer Vectorization:**
  - Model: `ProsusAI/finbert` (local open-source financial sentiment transformer).
  - Output: Continuous probability scores `[negative, neutral, positive]` mapped to a single polarity index $[-1.0, +1.0]$.
